## Priority Card, Part 1: The Priority Engine and the Card (2026-08-12)

The top of the Today screen now shows one thing: her single focus for today, one line explaining why, and three actions. Root decides what it is. Part 2 will deepen the motion design; this build delivers the selection engine and a fully working card with a deliberately simple entrance.

**No new engine was built.** This is a decision layer over systems that already shipped. Every input is read through the owning system's own published accessor:

| Rule | Existing system it reads |
| --- | --- |
| 0. Re-entry (override) | `lib/return-greeting/` (Root Presence, migration 143) + `session_started` events from the migration 146 analytics pipeline |
| 1. Reset Plan commitment not completed today | `lib/reset-plan/data.ts`, `lib/reset-plan/actionLibrary.ts` (migration 142) |
| 2. Strongly implicated, goal-relevant driver | `lib/case-view/investigation.ts` over `lib/driver-library/` + `lib/correlation-engine/`; reason sentence from `lib/case-view/findings.ts` |
| 3. Incomplete high-value action | `lib/assessment-registry/facts.ts` (the `assessment_status_by_member` view) + the Reset Plan's own `draft` state |
| 4. Today's Focus | the Coaching Brain's decision, passed in by the page that already fetched it |

Nothing here computes a correlation, a driver state, a trend, a score, or a content selection. `lib/case-view/investigation.ts`'s `likelyInvolved` bucket is reused verbatim for rule 2 rather than re-deriving goal relevance, so Case View and the Priority Card can never disagree about what Root is looking at, and `'watching'` is structurally unable to reach the card.

### Re-entry and Root Presence were unified, not stacked

The brief's hard requirement was one coherent welcome, never a greeting from one system plus a competing takeover from another. Root Presence already greets on a **3-day check-in gap**; re-entry takes over on **7+ days of sign-in absence**. Those measure different things, and side by side they would have produced exactly that incoherence.

`lib/return-greeting/absence.ts` is the reconciliation, deliberately placed **inside** the Root Presence module rather than beside it:

- Both thresholds live in one file. `RE_ENTRY_MIN_ABSENCE_DAYS = 7` is a named constant, and `classifyPresence` **calls** the existing `isEligibleForReturnGreeting` rather than restating the 3-day rule, so the greeting threshold still has exactly one definition anywhere in the codebase.
- There is still one greeting sentence in the product and one owner of it. The Priority Card **never writes `member_return_greetings`** and never authors a welcome line of its own; when re-entry fires, the card renders `RETURN_GREETING_TEXT`, the same sentence Root already says. `tests/priority-card-copy.test.ts` guards both facts against a real call or import, not a mention.
- A sign-in absence is treated as the same episode seen through a stronger signal, so it escalates the greeting rather than competing with it. Existing greeting behavior below 7 days is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Re-entry also suppresses the Past Lessons list, the one place on Today that labels old items "Not completed" — a member returning after a real absence is precisely who must not be handed a column of them. It clears once she engages with the card, and naturally on her next visit once a newer `session_started` exists.

### The card

Dominant first element of Today, above every other card including the first-check-in welcome, and guarded as such by a test. Not a modal, not a popup. Label, priority, one reason line, then Done / Help me / Save for later.

- **Done** marks the row done and the card moves to an accomplished state using the Today page's own accomplished language. When the priority is a Reset Plan commitment it also writes the plan's **real** `member_reset_plan_daily_logs` row, which is what genuinely feeds tomorrow: rule 1 asks "not completed today", so a logged completion is what stops the same commitment winning again before she has done it. Nothing decorative, no second copy of the Reset Plan's completion state.
- **Help me** expands in place with the easiest smaller step. No navigation, no round trip; the card contains no `useRouter`. The smaller step is reused from what already exists (the Reset Plan's own difficult-day version, the lesson's suggested action).
- **Save for later** collapses the card and relocates it below the day's zones, still available, and Root does not raise it back to dominant that day.

**No insight without a query.** Every reason line is `string | null` and is omitted entirely when no honest reason exists. A brand-new member gets the focus with no reason line at all, a Reset Plan on day one gets none, a driver with no goal-relevant earned finding gets none, and re-entry gets none **by construction and permanently**, because the only fact available there is the length of her absence and naming it is the guilt Root Presence exists to avoid.

### One thing the design got wrong first, and the fix

The first cut regenerated the card's text on every render. That is wrong: the winning rule legitimately changes **during** the day, because marking a Reset Plan commitment done is exactly what makes rule 1 stop applying. The accomplished card would then have shown a different priority than the one she had just completed. So `member_daily_priorities` stores `priority_title` and `priority_help` (stable content assembled from fixed libraries) and the stored row is authoritative, while the **reason line is deliberately never stored** and is always regenerated live or omitted. Derived insight stays live; the words she was actually shown stay fixed.

The service also fails closed: if the row cannot be claimed, it renders **no card** rather than one whose Done and Save buttons would silently do nothing.

### Migration 147 `priority_card`

One new table, `member_daily_priorities`, one row per member per local day with a real `unique (member_id, local_date)` constraint — "one winner, never two cards, never a list" enforced in the database, not only in the selection code. RLS scoped to `member_id = auth.uid()` with the usual coach and platform-administrator read paths.

Three additive analytics event types (`priority_shown`, `priority_action`, `re_entry_shown`) added by **widening** `member_wellness_events`' existing check constraint, the same rule migrations 63 and 146 set out, plus `is_product_analytics_event_type` recreated so the `product_analytics_events` view picks them up without changing. One new payload key, `rule`, a fixed slug from a closed allowlist. Payloads stay behavioral: which kind of thing won, never which driver, never its evidence, never the sentence shown.

### Testing

57 new tests across `tests/priority-hierarchy.test.ts` and `tests/priority-card-copy.test.ts`.

The precedence tests are built to be **non-vacuous by construction**: every one starts from a single fixture in which all five rules apply at once and removes only the rules above the one under test, then asserts via `applicableRules` that the losing rules really were available and really lost. This was verified by mutation, not assumed:

| Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Re-entry no longer overrides | 3 tests fail |
| Rule 2 promoted above rule 1 | 9 tests fail |
| Reason line no longer suppressed for a brand-new member | 1 test fails |

All three sources were restored and re-verified clean afterwards.

### Live verification on app.mefwellness.com (2026-08-12)

Deploy confirmed before testing: repo `MEFwellness/mef-platform`, branch `main`, Vercel project `mef-platform` (org `mef-wellness`), target **Production**, deployment `mef-platform-mlwe9xgb7`, status Ready, and `app.mefwellness.com` listed among its aliases via `vercel inspect`.

Pre-flight confirmed the table absent, the index name free, all 5 policy names free, and `has_active_role`/`is_active_coach_for` present. 12 statements, all succeeded. Post-checks: 13 columns, RLS enabled, 5 policies, 1 unique constraint, all three new event types accepted by `is_product_analytics_event_type`, and `product_analytics_events` still selectable. Recorded in the ledger; `db push --dry-run` reports **"Remote database is up to date."**

Driven with `scripts/screenshots/verify-priority-card-live.mjs`. **Zero console errors, zero page errors, zero 5xx across every account.**

#### memberPopulated — rule 1 won, and it was the right rule

Card rendered as **section 1 of 7**, the dominant first element, with exactly one card on the page and all three buttons.

- **Priority**: "See if you can catch the moment your energy dips today. Notice what was happening just before it changed. Then stand and roll your shoulders once." That is her own active Reset Plan's agreed action, verbatim from the action library (`energy` / `still_deciding`, plan active since 2026-08-02) — not a reworded copy.
- **Reason**: "You have logged this on 1 day since your plan started." Verified against the data: she had exactly one prior logged day (2026-08-02, `not_today`). The singular/plural branch is correct.
- **Help me**: expanded **in place**, still on `/today`, no navigation, revealing the plan's own difficult-day version: "Just catch the dip. Noticing it is enough."
- **Done**: card moved to the accomplished state, and it **persisted across a full reload** ("Done today.").
- **Done's real side effect confirmed in the database**: `member_reset_plan_daily_logs` gained `2026-08-12 / completed_normal`. That is the thing that genuinely feeds tomorrow's selection, since rule 1 asks "not completed today". Not decorative.
- No em dash in the card.

**Analytics, read back from production**: 3 x `priority_shown` `{"rule":"reset_plan_commitment"}`, plus `priority_action` `{"rule":"reset_plan_commitment","action":"help"}` and `priority_action` `{"rule":"reset_plan_commitment","action":"done"}`. Behavioral only, no health content, no priority text.

#### memberBelowThreshold and memberEmpty — no card, and the reason is upstream

Neither account rendered a card. The engine behaved **correctly and honestly**: every rule's input is genuinely absent for them, so `selectPriority` returned null rather than inventing a priority.

The specific cause is rule 4. Both accounts show the Today page's own **pre-existing** empty state, "Still putting today's lesson together." — the branch that renders when `decision.feedItem` is null, which existed before this build. Confirmed at the source: `daily_feed_items` contains **zero rows for all three test members**, including memberPopulated. The Coaching Brain has never produced a lesson for these accounts, so rule 4, the designed catch-all, has nothing to fall back to.

memberPopulated got a card only because rule 1 applied independently of the feed.

**This is a real gap worth a decision, not a defect in the priority engine.** The hierarchy's "otherwise, Today's Focus" branch is empty in production for exactly the early-days population the card is most meant to serve. Flagged rather than silently patched: adding a fifth fallback rule would widen the specified hierarchy, which is the product owner's call.

#### Not verified live, and why

- **Save for later** — needs a member with an active card today. memberPopulated's row is already `done` for 2026-08-12, and the other two have no card. Resetting the fixture requires a write to production test-account data, which the environment's safety classifier blocked.
- **Re-entry override** — needs a `session_started` row 7+ days old. Every test account's only sign-in rows are from today (artifacts of the migration-143 verification); memberEmpty has none at all. Seeding one backdated row for `test.member.belowthreshold` was blocked by the same classifier.

Both behaviors are covered by the local guard tests, and both remain unproven **on the live site**. Stated plainly rather than implied.

### Checks

`npm run typecheck` clean. `npm run lint` 0 errors (90 pre-existing `no-console` warnings, untouched). Production build compiles, 89/89 static pages. Full suite **3777/3778**.

The one failure, `tests/correlation-engine-integration.test.ts`, is **pre-existing and unrelated to this build** — proven by stashing this work and re-running: a clean tree fails **two** tests (that one plus `tests/assessment-runtime-integration.test.ts`), so this branch removes one failure and adds none. Root cause of the correlation one was found and partly fixed: two orphaned `daily_checkins` rows dated 2015-07-01 for `memberOne`, referenced by no test in the repo, sat inside the engine's 180-day lookback and added a 31st observation to a 30-day fixture. Deleting them makes that test pass in isolation; it still fails inside the full parallel run, which is a genuine pre-existing test-isolation problem between integration files sharing the `memberOne` fixture. Not fixed here, flagged.

**Pre-flight**: the target row still held the exact pre-migration string the migration's own guarded `WHERE` clause matches on.

Both recorded. Production now has an unbroken run from 134 through 146 with no gaps.

### Live proof that the Root Presence System is genuinely working now, not just present

Asserting the tables exist would prove almost nothing, so the real app was driven until it wrote a row on its own.

`test.member.belowthreshold@example.test` last checked in on 2026-07-29, a 14-day gap, comfortably past the 3-day threshold in `lib/return-greeting/gate.ts`. Logged into `app.mefwellness.com` as that account and loaded Home. **Root's no-guilt return line, "I'm glad you're back.", rendered on the live page**, and `member_return_greetings` gained exactly one real row: `gap_start_local_date = 2026-07-29`, the member's true last check-in date, timestamped at the moment of the visit. Zero console errors, zero page errors, zero 5xx.

**The one-greeting-per-gap guarantee was then tested, not assumed.** A second visit to Home left the table at exactly one row: the composite primary key blocked a second claim, which is the whole purpose of the table. The greeting text still appears on that second visit, and that is correct rather than a bug: `getOrCreateTodaysMorningBrief` caches one brief per member per local date, so today's already-created brief keeps its `encouraging_message` for the rest of the day. Confirmed directly in the data: that member's 2026-08-12 brief was created at the same instant as the greeting row and its `encouraging_message` is "I'm glad you're back.", while their 2026-08-11 brief (written before 143 existed) has ordinary streak copy instead.

That last detail is also the cleanest confirmation of the degradation the backfill entry predicted. Yesterday's brief got no greeting despite the same 14-day gap, because `tryMarkReturnGreetingShown` fails closed when its table is missing and so never returned true. Today, with the table in place, the greeting fired on the first eligible page load. The feature really was inert in production, and really is live now.

`member_discovery_moments` is created and correct but still empty, which is expected: it only gains rows when a member is shown a brand-new correlation-finding discovery, and no such discovery came up during this check.

### No regression

Re-checked `memberPopulated` afterwards: login landed on Home, Home returned 200 with its real personalized heading, and the Daily Reset screen returned 200 with its heading, first question block, and working Continue button. Zero errors of any kind. No code changed in this task, so nothing was built or deployed.

**One pre-existing behavior worth noting, not caused by this task**: logging in as `memberBelowThreshold` lands on `/name` rather than Home, because that account has no `display_name` and `resolvePostLoginPath` redirects until one is set. That is the intended behavior shipped in the Member Fixes Batch entry below.

## Production Migration Ledger Backfill (2026-08-12)

Ledger-only task. Production's `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` recorded migrations only through `00000000000134` (plus `146`), even though most of 135 through 145 had genuinely been applied by hand through the SQL Editor. That gap made `supabase db push` unusable against production: it would have tried to re-run already-applied migrations and failed. This task made the ledger match reality. **No migration SQL was re-run and no schema object was created, altered, or dropped.** The only writes were `insert into supabase_migrations.schema_migrations (version, name)` rows.

Each migration was verified against production first, one at a time, and recorded only after its effects were confirmed fully present. Verification was per-migration, derived from reading each file and checking every object or data change it creates, not a single spot check.

### Recorded (9 of 11), with the proof used for each

## Product Analytics Instrumentation (2026-08-11)

Behavioral product tracking, built by extending the event pipeline this platform already had rather than adding a second one or a third-party SDK. Full reference, including every query pattern, lives in `docs/PRODUCT_ANALYTICS.md`.

### Audit first: what already existed

`member_wellness_events` (migration 63) was already the shared, payload-bearing event table, with `lib/events/service.ts`'s `recordMemberEvent` as its single write path and an explicit rule in its own header comment: "a future event source widens this check constraint, never adds a second events table." That is exactly what this task did. Four other event-ish tables were checked and deliberately left alone: `health_timeline_events` (a member-facing milestone story feed, not analytics), `ai_events` (AI dispatcher inputs), `member_recommendation_events` (per-recommendation outcome history), and `investigation_router_decisions`. No third-party analytics tool existed and none was added.

Of the ten things the brief asked for, three were already captured in some form and were reused rather than duplicated:

- **Onboarding completion** already wrote a `health_timeline_events` row (`onboarding_completed`) and an AI event (`member_completed_onboarding`). Both kept, untouched; the new `onboarding_completed` analytics event sits alongside them because neither of the existing two is queryable as behavior (one is member-facing narrative, the other is dispatcher input) and neither has a matching "started" event.
- **Daily Reset completion** already wrote a `morning_readiness_recorded` wellness event pointing at the real check-in row. Kept, untouched; the new `daily_reset_completed` carries no answer content at all and is what an analytics query reads.
- **Today's Focus view** already had `markTodaysFeedOpened`, called once per real page view from `FeedInteractions`'s mount effect. Reused as the trigger for the view event rather than adding a second one that could double count.

Everything else (signup, sessions, surface views, Daily Reset start, Food Lens scans, food entries, Reset Plan engagement, paywall views, tier changes) had no behavioral event at all.

### What was added

**Migration 146** (`00000000000146_product_analytics_events.sql`) widens `member_wellness_events.event_type` with thirteen behavioral types, adds a `(event_type, occurred_at desc)` index for cross-member analytics slicing (the two existing member-scoped indexes cannot serve it and are untouched), and adds `product_analytics_events`, a `security_invoker` view that excludes the five health-content wellness types by construction and joins `profiles.is_test` onto every row so test accounts filter out with a plain `where is_test = false`. Test-account events still write normally, exactly as the brief asked.

Two events are written by the database rather than the app, because neither has an authenticated app request to hang off: `signup_completed` extends `handle_new_user()` (at signup there is no session yet, so an app-side insert would be rejected by RLS), and `membership_tier_changed` is a new trigger on `profiles.membership_tier`. Both are wrapped in their own exception blocks so an analytics failure can never break a signup or a profile update.

**`lib/analytics/track.ts`** is a thin, never-throwing wrapper over `recordMemberEvent`. It returns `false` on failure instead of rejecting, so `await` on a member-facing path is always safe. **`lib/analytics/surfaces.ts`** holds closed allowlists for every value a payload may carry. **`app/actions/analytics.ts`** exposes the four server actions client components call, each validating against those allowlists (values arrive from the browser, so validation is what makes smuggling health content impossible). **`components/analytics/TrackSurfaceView.tsx`** renders `null` and fires from a mount effect, so page views are recorded after paint and never delay a server render, with a module-level dedupe window so React's development double-effect and rapid re-mounts cannot double count.

Thirteen event types now tracked: `signup_completed`, `session_started`, `onboarding_started`, `onboarding_completed`, `surface_viewed` (19 surfaces), `daily_reset_started`, `daily_reset_completed`, `food_scan_performed`, `food_entry_logged`, `feature_engaged` (Today's Focus and Reset Plan), `paywall_viewed`, `membership_tier_changed`, and `purchase_completed` (defined, nothing emits it, see below).

`food_entry_logged` is recorded inside `lib/food-products/data.ts`'s `insertFoodLogEntry`, the one function all six logging paths already funnel through, rather than at each call site, so the count is complete by construction and a future logging path cannot silently go untracked.

### The hard line: behavioral only

No analytics payload can carry health content. Enforced in three places, not by convention: the allowlists reject any surface/feature/action/lock-reason that is not a known slug; `sanitizeAnalyticsPayload` drops every key outside a fixed twelve-key list and every value over 48 characters (all legitimate values are short slugs, prose is the shape health content arrives in); and `tests/product-analytics-payload-safety.test.ts` parses every analytics call site in `app/`, `lib/`, and `components/` and fails on any payload key outside the allowlist or on any obviously health-adjacent field name.

### Purchases: honestly, not capturable yet

There is no billing integration in this codebase. No Stripe SDK, no webhook endpoint, no checkout route, and nothing anywhere that writes `profiles.membership_tier` (verified by grep: it is read in five places and written in none). `/membership` lists what a membership includes and points at a support email. Trial, monthly, annual, and 24-week checkout all happen outside this application, so this application has nothing to observe. Rather than fake it: `membership_tier_changed` captures the effect of a purchase (every real tier movement, however it is made) via the database trigger, `paywall_viewed` captures the demand side, and `purchase_completed` exists as an accepted type with a defined payload that nothing emits. When billing moves in-app, it is one `trackProductEvent` call with no schema change.

### Return frequency

Not a new mechanism, per the brief. `session_started` is the raw event, written by both the password and passkey sign-in paths. Daily/weekly actives and days-between-visits are derived queries, all documented with runnable SQL in `docs/PRODUCT_ANALYTICS.md`, including the `distinct member_id, local_date` collapse so three sign-ins in one day count as one visit.

### Tests

`tests/product-analytics-events.test.ts` (26 tests, real local Supabase, no mocks): every new type is accepted by the widened constraint and rejected if misspelled; member id and both timestamps land on every event; creating a real auth user writes exactly one `signup_completed` with `source = 'system'`; a real tier change writes exactly one `membership_tier_changed` with the true from/to tiers and a no-op update writes none; the view exposes analytics events and provably excludes a `concern_flagged` row's text; `is_test` events still write and are excludable; return frequency comes out of the raw events; a sanitized payload really is what reaches the database; and a rejected write returns `false` rather than throwing. Both database-written tests use throwaway accounts they create and delete, not the seeded members, because other test files in the same run also write those members' tiers.

`tests/product-analytics-payload-safety.test.ts` (5 tests): the source scan described above, with its own non-vacuity proof against a known-bad fixture.

**Guard proven non-vacuous by actually breaking it**: the `trackProductEvent` call was removed from `submitDailyCheckin`, both files re-run (2 tests failed for the right reason: the missing call site and the call-count floor), then restored and re-run clean (`git diff --stat` confirms the restored file is exactly the intended 15-line addition).

### Zero member-facing change

No copy, no markup, no layout, no styling changed anywhere. Every tracking component renders `null`. The only edits to existing UI files are one self-closing tracker element and one import.

### Verified

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Repo-root `npm run lint`: 0 errors, same 90 pre-existing warnings, none in new or touched files. Full `npx vitest run` after a fresh `supabase db reset` through migration 146: 325/326 test files, 3720/3721 tests passing. The one failure is the same pre-existing `tests/correlation-engine-integration.test.ts` Spearman observation-count flake documented throughout this file's history, reconfirmed unrelated by running it in isolation on a fresh database both with this change (passes) and with the change stashed (passes) while failing in both full-suite runs. `npm run build` compiled successfully, every route generated.

### Migration status: APPLIED to production

Migration 146 is applied to production and recorded in the migration ledger. Applied 2026-08-12 via a direct `psql` connection over the pooler (`--db-url` pattern, per this project's established practice), in a single transaction with `ON_ERROR_STOP`, after pre-flight checks confirmed the old constraint existed, no tier-change trigger existed, `profiles.is_test`/`membership_tier` were both present, and production's `handle_new_user()` was byte-identical to migration 85's version before being replaced. All ten statements succeeded (2 ALTER TABLE, 1 CREATE INDEX, 3 CREATE FUNCTION, 1 CREATE VIEW, 1 COMMENT, 1 CREATE TRIGGER, 1 NOTIFY). Confirmed live afterwards: `handle_new_user()` contains the signup analytics insert, `track_membership_tier_change_trigger` exists and is enabled, and `product_analytics_events` is queryable.

**A real, unrelated finding worth acting on separately.** Production's migration ledger only recorded up to `00000000000134`. Migrations 135 through 145 were missing from it, but spot checks confirmed three of their schema objects (`member_reset_plans`, `member_root_popup_dismissals`, `assessment_assignments`) genuinely exist in production, suggesting those migrations were applied by hand through the SQL Editor and simply never recorded. **Corrected 2026-08-12 by the Migration Ledger Backfill entry above: that generalization was wrong. Nine of the eleven were applied; 143 and 145 were not applied at all.** This is why `supabase db push` must NOT be used against this project as-is: it would try to re-run eleven already-applied migrations and fail. That is exactly why 146 was applied as a single explicit file rather than through `db push`. Only 146 was added to the ledger; back-filling ledger rows for 135 through 145 is a separate cleanup, and it should be done after verifying each one object by object, not assumed from the three that were spot-checked.

### Live-site verification (production, app.mefwellness.com)

Deployed from the repo root (`vercel --prod`, deployment `dpl_FSy5hcSirootVJKU5pWxjgtSX6jG`, target production, status Ready, aliased to `app.mefwellness.com` alongside `mef-platform.vercel.app`). Repo `MEFwellness/mef-platform`, branch `main`, Vercel project `mef-platform`, all confirmed before and after. `curl -I https://app.mefwellness.com` returns the expected 307 to `/login` and `/login` returns 200 from this deployment. Note: a first `vercel --prod` run from inside `apps/consumer-web-app` failed with "Couldn't find any pages or app directory" because the project's Root Directory setting already points at that subdirectory; deploying from the repo root is correct and is what shipped.

`scripts/screenshots/verify-product-analytics-live.mjs` (new) drove the real member journey on production as `memberPopulated`: password login, Home, Daily Reset (opened AND fully completed, four screens through submit and the ending screen), Food Lens, Progress, Your Wellness Story, Today, Your Case, Movement, Questionnaires, and Membership. **11 of 11 steps passed, with zero console errors, zero page errors, and zero 5xx responses.**

**The production event table was then queried, and every action produced exactly the expected event, once, with the right type, payload, and member id.** Fourteen rows, in journey order: `session_started {method: password}`, `surface_viewed {home}` (twice, correctly: once from the post-login redirect onto Home and once from the explicit second navigation to it, six seconds apart and genuinely two visits), `surface_viewed {daily_reset}`, `daily_reset_started`, `daily_reset_completed`, then `surface_viewed` for `food_lens`, `progress`, `today`, `your_case`, `movement`, `questionnaires`, and `membership`, and finally `paywall_viewed {feature: membership, lockReason: membership}`. No `paywall_viewed` fired on Questionnaires, which is correct: that account is on a paid tier, so no card there is tier-locked for them.

**Every payload was behavioral only.** No answer content, no pain location, no sleep number, nothing from the Daily Reset that was just completed, despite that check-in having been submitted for real.

**`is_test` filtering confirmed working on live data.** All fourteen journey rows carry `is_test = true`. The production table currently holds 17 analytics rows total; `where is_test = false` returns the 3 written by real members and correctly excludes all 14 test rows. Test-account events still write normally, exactly as the brief required.

**Every documented query in `docs/PRODUCT_ANALYTICS.md` was run against production and returns.**

**One real defect found and fixed during live verification.** The first production query returned zero rows, because `occurred_at` is not a true UTC instant: `nowInTimezone` (`lib/time/localDate.ts`) stamps the member's wall clock as UTC, which is exactly what makes `local_date` come out right and is how every row in this table has always been written, including the five pre-existing wellness types. This is a long-standing platform convention, not something this task introduced, but it silently broke four of the documented analytics queries, which filtered `occurred_at >= now() - interval '30 days'` and would have quietly under-counted by the timezone offset near every boundary. All of them now group and filter on `local_date` (the member's real calendar day, correct as written) and the two that genuinely need clock instants (returned-within-7-days-of-signup) now use `recorded_at`, the true server write time. `docs/PRODUCT_ANALYTICS.md` documents the convention and which column to reach for in which case, with the observed production values as the worked example. Had this only been tested locally in UTC, it would never have surfaced.

This also resolves the open question the entries below left about migrations 144 and 145: `assessment_assignments` (144) was confirmed present in production during this task's pre-flight checks, so that migration's schema really is applied, it was just never recorded in the ledger. 145 is copy-only and was not separately verified.

## Coach-Assign-Only Gating: visible-locked treatment + Body Assessment closed (2026-08-04)

Registry questionnaires were already assignment-gated as of the "Assignment-Gated Questionnaires" task (2026-08-03, below) for five of the eight tools this request names — but that task made a gated item **invisible** until assigned, not **visibly locked**, and it deliberately left Body Assessment (the camera-based posture/movement capture flow) completely open to any member. This task closes both gaps: (1) invisible-until-assigned becomes visible-and-locked (dimmed card, gold corner marker, tap-to-reveal Root-voice note) everywhere a gated item can appear, and (2) Body Assessment joins the same `requiresAssignment` gate as the other five, with every real entry point into its flow (not just the obvious ones) closed server-side.

**Reused, not rebuilt**: the entire gating substrate already existed — `requiresAssignment`, `calculateLockReason`/`checkAssessmentAccess` (real server-side enforcement), `categorizeForCatalog`, the `assessment_assignments` coach-assign mechanism (`assignAssessmentAction`, `AssessmentAssignmentPanel.tsx`), and the Root pop-up chain (`questionnaire_assigned` kind, `member_root_popup_dismissals`). Nothing here is a second gating system — this task changed what the existing one does (hidden -> locked-visible) and where it applies (5 items -> 8), and reused every existing rendering/notification surface rather than building new ones. No new migration was needed: Body Assessment already had a real `assessment_definitions` row (from the original registry work) and the completion-tracking trigger (migration 144) already covered it as one of its five convergent sources — only `lib/assessment-registry/registry.ts`'s own `requiresAssignment` flag needed to flip.

### 1. Hidden -> locked-visible (the explicit "not hiding" requirement)

`categorizeForCatalog` (`lib/assessment-registry/catalog.ts`) used to return a `hidden` section for a `requiresAssignment` item nobody had assigned yet — the Questionnaires catalog action (`getMyQuestionnaireCatalog`) skipped building a card for it entirely, so a member saw nothing. `CatalogSection` no longer has a `hidden` member at all: an unassigned gated item now falls straight into `calculateLockReason`'s own pre-existing `not_assigned` branch, landing in its normal Available/Premium section with `flags.locked = true` and a new `flags.lockReasonKind` (`'not_assigned' | 'membership' | 'program_enrollment' | 'program_phase' | 'prerequisite' | null`) so the UI can tell a coach-assignment lock apart from a membership-tier lock — only the former gets the new dimmed/gold-marker/tap-to-reveal treatment; a membership lock keeps its existing "Locked" pill + "View Membership" prompt, unchanged. A Coming Soon, assignment-gated placeholder (Readiness to Change, Finding 1 Love — see below) now shows as an ordinary "Coming Soon" card again instead of being invisible.

**New shared primitives** (`components/locked/`): `CoachLockBadge.tsx` (a small gold #C4A050 circular corner marker with a lock icon, positioned outside whatever opacity wrapper dims the rest of the card so the marker itself never dims) and `LockedCardButton.tsx` (wraps a locked card's content in a real `<button>`; tapping it never navigates, it opens `NoticingSheet` — the app's one existing "tap something, get a short message" bottom-sheet primitive, already used by the dashboard's Noticing carousel — with a short, warm, first-person Root note: *"This one opens once your coach assigns it to you. I'll let you know the moment it's ready."*, `lib/locked-content/copy.ts`, no em dash, no pressure language). `components/questionnaires/CatalogQuestionnaireCard.tsx` (the `/questionnaires` catalog, reached from Home's Questionnaires summary card and Wellness Story's Explore section) now renders every coach-assign-only-locked card through these two primitives instead of hiding it.

### 2. Body Assessment closed, every real entry point audited

`BODY_ASSESSMENT.requiresAssignment` flipped `false` -> `true`. Server-side enforcement, not UI-only:
- `app/assessment/page.tsx` (the overview/history page) now calls `checkAssessmentAccess` and, when denied, replaces the whole page with a graceful locked card (same `CenterStage` pattern the generic engine's own overview page already used for this) instead of the type-picker + history — never an error page or a crash. `checkAssessmentAccess` always lets a member with real history or a pending assignment through (never hides existing progress), so a denial here only happens for a member with genuinely nothing to see anyway.
- `app/assessment/new/page.tsx` (the take flow) checks access and redirects to `/assessment` on denial, same "take page redirects to the overview, which owns the message" pattern the generic engine's take page already used.
- `app/actions/body-assessment.ts`'s `startAssessmentAction` — the actual write path that creates a `body_assessments` row — checks access too, before ever inserting, so a direct call (bypassing both pages) is still blocked. This is the defense-in-depth layer: the two pages above are what a member actually hits, this is what stops someone who didn't.

**Audited every route into the flow, not just the obvious one**: `MovementAssessmentCard.tsx` (the "Guided Posture & Movement Assessment" invite card shown on Home), the "Assessments" row in Wellness Story's Explore section (`app/progress/page.tsx`), and the "Assessments" card on the Profile page (`app/profile/page.tsx`) — the three real entry points a grep for `/assessment`/`/assessment/new` across `app/` and `components/` turned up. All three now render the same locked treatment (dimmed, gold corner marker, tap-to-reveal note) when `checkAssessmentAccess('body-assessment')` denies, instead of linking through. **One clarification for the record**: the dashboard's Quick Actions "Movement" pill (`components/dashboard/QuickActionsGrid.tsx`) was checked and does **not** lead into Body Assessment at all — its `href` is `/movement`, the separate, unrelated Movement Intelligence workout hub (`app/movement/page.tsx`, exercise sessions), which has zero links into `/assessment` anywhere on it. That pill was deliberately left untouched; gating it would have locked free members out of a genuinely different, ungated feature nobody asked to gate. If the intended target really was that literal pill, say so and it's a quick follow-up — but the big gold "Start Assessment" invite card on Home (which does start the camera flow directly) is now locked, which is almost certainly the button being described.

### 3. Assigned state: unlocks, top priority, pop-up — reused end to end

Body Assessment was `assignmentSupported: true` in the registry already, but `listAssignableAssessments()` (the source of the coach's assignment dropdown, `AssessmentAssignmentPanel.tsx`) explicitly excluded it ("its own dedicated capture/review system"). That exclusion is gone — a coach can now assign it exactly like any of the other seven, through the same existing dropdown, same `assignAssessmentAction`, same `assessment_assignments` table.

The Questionnaires catalog (`getMyQuestionnaireCatalog`) still deliberately excludes Body Assessment from `/questionnaires` and its counts — that product decision predates this task and wasn't reopened. Instead, a new sibling function, `getMyBodyAssessmentAssignmentCard()` (`app/actions/questionnaireCatalog.ts`), builds the same `CatalogCard` shape only when a pending assignment exists, and two existing consumers merge it in without touching the excluded catalog: `DashboardInviteCards.tsx` folds it into the same array `AssignedQuestionnairePriorityCard` already renders (so an assigned Body Assessment gets the identical dark forest-green/gold top-priority card every other coach assignment gets), and `rootPopupMessages.ts` folds it into the same `assignmentCandidates` list `findMyPendingRootPopupMessage()` already picks from — so it reuses the existing `questionnaire_assigned` pop-up kind verbatim (no new pop-up kind, no new dismissal machinery), correctly competing in the same priority waterfall as every other message.

### 4. Readiness to Change and Finding 1 Love: honest status, not built out

Both were already `requiresAssignment: true` Coming Soon placeholders with zero question content, no route, no scoring adapter (`implementationStatus: 'coming_soon'`, `takeRoute: null`) — this predates this task. They now render visibly as "Coming Soon" (previously invisible, per section 1 above), but **a coach still cannot meaningfully assign either one today**: `listAssignableAssessments()` correctly still excludes them (`implementationStatus !== 'live'`), because assigning something with no real content behind it would mean a member taps "Start now" on a Root pop-up and lands nowhere. Building the actual question content for these two is a real, separate content task (question bank, scoring, results presentation) — well outside an access-gating change — so it wasn't attempted here. **Per the explicit report requirement**: of the eight, six (Four Doctors, Nutrition & Lifestyle, Primal Pattern, WBSA, Short-HAQ, Body Assessment) are fully live and assignable today; Readiness to Change and Finding 1 Love are gated correctly in the registry but have no real flow yet for a coach to assign a member into.

### Tests

`tests/coach-assign-only-gating.test.ts` (new, real local Supabase, no mocks) — for all eight items: a brand-new member with zero assignments is denied server-side access with reason `not_assigned`, and a real inserted `assessment_assignments` row unlocks it, proven non-vacuous by temporarily reverting Body Assessment's `requiresAssignment` flag to `false`, re-running, watching the three Body-Assessment-specific assertions fail for the right reason, then restoring (diffed byte-identical) and re-running clean. ## Member Fixes Batch: name greeting, Daily Reset rename, onboarding polish, pop-up discoverability (2026-08-03)

Five independent member-facing fixes requested in one batch, implemented together, gated behind one all-or-nothing typecheck/lint/test/build pass per the task's own instructions.

### FIX 1 — Members were never asked for their name

Root cause: `profiles.display_name` was always optional (a "Skip for now" link on `app/name/page.tsx`), and 16 separate call sites across the app fell back to the literal word `'there'` (`profile?.display_name?.split(' ')[0] ?? 'there'`) whenever it was null — this is what produced "Good afternoon, there."

**New member flow**: unchanged in shape, tightened in behavior — `/name` already ran before the welcome flow's goal screen (via `app/api/auth/callback/route.ts`'s post-verification redirect), so the "ask early, before goals" requirement was already met structurally. What changed: the "Skip for now" link is gone (`app/name/NameForm.tsx`) — the field is now genuinely required, not just marked `required` on a skippable form.

**Existing member flow**: `lib/auth/postLoginRoute.ts`'s `resolvePostLoginPath()` now queries `profiles.display_name` right after the coach/admin role checks (before the welcome-flow/consent checks, so it's still "early") and redirects to `/name` whenever it's null — on every login, until answered, exactly the same one-time-prompt shape `/name`'s own existing guard (`redirect('/') once display_name is set`) already provides for new members. No new page needed, no new table — reused the existing screen and its existing guard.

**The greeting itself**: new `lib/profile/greeting.ts` — `firstNameFrom(displayName)` returns the real first name or `null` (never a placeholder), `greetingHeadline(greetingWord, firstName)` renders `"Good afternoon, Sarah"` when a name exists or `"Good afternoon."` (period, no comma) when it doesn't, exactly the fallback the task specified. All 16 `?? 'there'` call sites across `app/` and `lib/` now use `firstNameFrom`, and every place a name renders as user-visible text (the dashboard hero, `AvatarLink`/`ProfileSheet`'s avatar initial and name line, the coach dashboard's own greeting, `FirstCheckinTransition`, `MovementEmptyState`, `lib/feed/copy.ts`'s `buildCoachNote`) now branches on `null` instead of ever printing `'there'`. Two call sites that only feed a non-rendered DB column (`morning_briefs.greeting_name`, per `MorningBriefCard.tsx`'s own comment that the greeting is never repeated there) or an LLM prompt context line (`lib/conversation-coach/prompt.ts`, which now omits the "- Name:" line entirely when null, same conditional-line pattern that file already used for `entryContext`/`coachingStyleGuidance`) got the narrower, contained fix rather than full `string | null` propagation, since neither is directly member-visible.

**Avatar fallback**: `AvatarLink`/`ProfileSheet`/`app/profile/page.tsx` show a generic Lucide `User` icon instead of a name-initial letter when no name is on file (was rendering `'T'` for "there" before).

**Tests**: `tests/greeting-no-placeholder-guard.test.ts` — unit tests for `firstNameFrom`/`greetingHeadline`, plus a repo-wide static-scan guard (same convention as `tests/no-em-dash-guard.test.ts`) asserting zero `?? 'there'` fallbacks remain in `app/`/`components/`/`lib/`, proven non-vacuous (the detection regex is asserted against both a known-bad fixture string and a known-good one before the real scan runs).

### FIX 2 — "Morning Readiness" renamed to "Daily Reset"

Display-text-only rename across every member- and coach-facing spot the words appeared: the check-in header (`app/checkin/page.tsx`), the mode-switch nav pill (`components/checkin/CheckInModeSwitch.tsx`), the dashboard's Today's Wellness label (`components/checkin/DailyWellnessSection.tsx`), onboarding's completion screen copy and button (`OnboardingCompletionScreen.tsx`), the guest journey-preview copy (`lib/onboarding/journeyPreview.ts`), the evening reflection's cross-reference line, and four coach-admin question-bank screens (kept in sync so a coach configuring "which screen" a question appears on reads the same name a member now sees). Database columns, table names, question keys, and the internal `screen: 'morning'`/function names like `calculateMorningReadinessScore` are all untouched, per the task's explicit instruction — confirmed by grep: every remaining `morning`-named identifier in the codebase is a comment or internal code reference, never rendered text.

**Question copy swept for morning-assumption wording**: `app/checkin/CheckinForm.tsx`'s three feeling-section questions ("this morning" → "right now"), and one DB-stored question prompt, `checkin_probe.morning_soreness` ("How sore does your body feel this morning?" → "...right now?") — fixed via a new data-only migration (`00000000000145_daily_reset_rename_copy_sweep.sql`) rather than editing app code, since this text is coach-editable at runtime via `/coach/questions`. The `UPDATE` is guarded by a `WHERE prompt = '<original text>'` clause so it can never silently overwrite a coach's own edit made since migration 109. Every other check-in question already used past-tense ("last night") or day-neutral ("today") phrasing and needed no change.

### FIX 3 — "Onboarding already complete" page rebuilt

`app/onboarding/page.tsx`'s bare heading-and-paragraph state (two underlined text links, pinned to the top of the viewport) now uses `CenterStage` (Screen Layout System, Prompt 2 — the same component `OnboardingCompletionScreen.tsx` and `app/profile/reassessments/new/page.tsx` already use for this exact class of bug) and two real buttons: "Go to today's check-in" (solid dark green pill, primary) and "Review your Baseline Assessment" (outlined pill, secondary). Swept the rest of the file for the same bare-top-pinned bug: `UnavailableNotice` (the guest "We'll be right with you" state) shared it and is now also wrapped in `CenterStage`. The consent gate was deliberately left as-is — it holds a real multi-section form with a validation error that can appear/grow, exactly the case `CenterStage`'s own header comment says not to center.

**Tests**: `tests/onboarding-already-complete-layout.test.ts`, a source-scan (SSR component tests don't work in this repo) proving the block is `CenterStage`-wrapped, uses the two named buttons (not underlined links), and links to the right two routes.

### FIX 4 — Native dropdown replaced with tappable cards

Onboarding's one boolean (Yes/No) question type rendered as a native `<select>` (`app/onboarding/OnboardingForm.tsx`), which on a phone opens the OS picker directly over the question text. Replaced with the same `EnumOptionTile` tappable full-width cards every enum question in onboarding already uses, one column so both options stay full-width regardless of screen size. Audited the rest of onboarding and both check-in flows for any other native `<select>`/dropdown: none found — this was the only one, and every boolean-typed question across all 18 concern banks funnels through this one shared branch, so this single fix covers all of them, not just question 13 specifically (there is no fixed "question 13" — the adaptive engine mixes concern-specific and shared-pool questions, so a different boolean question can land at that position depending on the member's concern).

**Tests**: `tests/no-native-select-onboarding-checkin-guard.test.ts` — source-scan guard (comment-aware, so it doesn't false-positive on its own explanatory comments) proving zero native `<select>` elements remain in `app/onboarding`, `app/checkin`, or `components/checkin`, plus a direct check that the boolean branch renders `EnumOptionTile` radio cards.

### FIX 5 — Questionnaires and experiences now reach members as pop-ups, not just dashboard cards

Extended the existing Root pop-up chain (`app/actions/rootPopupMessages.ts`, `components/dashboard/RootMessagePopupClient.tsx`, `member_root_popup_dismissals` — migration 137, unchanged) rather than building a second mechanism, per the task's explicit instruction.

**New pop-up kind, `free_arc_available`**: the next unstarted conversation among Core Values Snapshot, Life Signal Check, and Readiness Pulse. New `lib/root-popup-messages/freeArc.ts` walks the registry's own real prerequisite chain (`FREE_ARC_SEQUENCE`, matching `lib/assessment-registry/registry.ts`'s `displayOrder`) and picks the first not-yet-completed one — since prerequisites are sequential and match this exact order, the first not-completed key is always unlocked by construction, no separate lock check needed. Checked last in the priority waterfall (lowest priority of everything there): an invitation to start something new never preempts continuing something already active.

**Real, confirmed bug fixed**: a brand-new member (completed onboarding, zero check-ins) had **no reachable path at all** — card or pop-up — to any of the three free conversations, because `app/dashboard/page.tsx`'s `!hasCheckins` gate hid the entire "Your Path" zone (the only place `/questionnaires` was linked from), and the pop-up itself was separately gated behind `hasCheckins` too. Fixed two ways: (1) new `components/dashboard/DashboardInviteCards.tsx` (replacing the old, narrower `AssignedQuestionnairePriorityCard`-only block) renders both the coach-assignment card and a new `FreeArcInviteCard` unconditionally at the top of `<main>`, above the `hasCheckins` gate — the same "always reachable" precedent the assignment card already established; (2) the `hasCheckins &&` condition was removed from the Root pop-up's own pass-through in `app/dashboard/page.tsx` (the wearable-prompt gate is untouched — today's real recovery numbers have nothing to show pre-first-check-in, a genuinely different case). This also fixes reachability for case 2 (a coach-assigned questionnaire's pop-up, previously also silently blocked for a zero-check-in member) and, once a member completes their first free-arc conversation, case 3 (the "start the weekly experiment" offer pop-ups, `cvs_offer`/`lsc_offer`/`rpl_offer` — these already existed in the chain and needed no new kind, since "newly unlocked experience" and "just finished the underlying conversation" are the same real trigger these offers already fire on).

**Button behavior fixed to match the task's spec**: `questionnaire_assigned` previously auto-marked itself dismissed the instant it mounted (a true one-time-ever pop-up, regardless of which button was tapped) — this contradicted the task's explicit "Maybe later snoozes and returns next login, Ignore is permanent" requirement. Both `questionnaire_assigned` and the new `free_arc_available` now use the same recurring `isRootPopupDueThisLogin` semantics day-3/day-7 messages already use, with real "Maybe later"/"Ignore" buttons (new shared `RootInvitePopup` component, replacing the old `QuestionnaireAssignedPopup`). The "Waiting on you" gold badge (previously only wired for CVS/LSC/RPL experiment cards) now also appears on `AssignedQuestionnairePriorityCard` and `FreeArcInviteCard` once their own pop-up has been snoozed, read from the same `member_root_popup_dismissals` row the pop-up itself checks.

**Priority order, as promised in the task**: coach-assigned questionnaire (highest — a direct coach action) → CVS day3 → day7 → offer → LSC day3 → day7 → offer → RPL day3 → day7 → offer → Personal Reset Plan day3 → day7 → free-arc-available (lowest — an invitation to something new). One pop-up per login, never during onboarding/signup (structurally impossible — the pop-up only renders from `/dashboard`, unreachable until onboarding is complete), never alongside another pop-up (`HomeScreenPopups`'s existing single-slot arbitration, unchanged).

**Tests**: `tests/free-arc-popup.test.ts` (pure `pickNextFreeArcCard` sequencing: picks CVS for zero-history, LSC once CVS is done, RPL once both are done, null once all three are done, never skips ahead past an incomplete prerequisite). Extended `tests/root-popup-messages.test.ts` with a new describe block proving the recurring-semantics switch is real: a snoozed assignment candidate is skipped the same login but due again after a later login, an ignored one never comes back.

### Verified

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Repo-root `npm run lint` — 0 errors, same 90 pre-existing warnings (none in touched/new files, confirmed by grep against the lint output). ## Assignment-Gated Questionnaires (2026-08-03)

Registry questionnaires (Four Doctors, Nutrition & Lifestyle, Primal Pattern, Short-HAQ, WBSA, plus the two Coming Soon placeholders) moved from openly-visible-to-any-member to invisible-until-a-coach-assigns-them. The three free experiences (Core Values Snapshot, Life Signal Check, Readiness Pulse), Onboarding, Body Assessment, Daily Check-In, Personal Reset Plan, experiments, and the 88-question coach bank are all untouched, per the task's own scope.

**Reused, not rebuilt, per the completion workflow's own instruction to say so**: the coach-assign mechanism (`assessment_assignments` table, migration 77; `assignAssessmentAction`/`cancelAssessmentAssignmentAction`, `app/actions/assessmentAssignments.ts`; the coach UI, `app/coach/clients/[id]/AssessmentAssignmentPanel.tsx`) already existed and already let a coach assign any registered questionnaire to a client with a reason/due date — this task did not rebuild it, only closed two real gaps in it (below) and reused it for the new visibility rule. The Root pop-up chain (`member_root_popup_dismissals`, migration 137; `app/actions/rootPopupMessages.ts`; `RootMessagePopupClient.tsx`) already existed too; this task added one new message kind to it rather than a second notification system.

**New `requiresAssignment` field** (`lib/assessment-registry/types.ts`/`registry.ts`) marks exactly the 7 gated entries (`chek-hlc1-nutrition-lifestyle`, `four-doctors`, `primal-pattern-diet-type`, `short-haq`, `wbsa`, `readiness-to-change`, `finding-1-love`) `true`; Onboarding, Body Assessment, and the three free experiences stay `false`. A single gate, checked in both `calculateLockReason` (`status.ts`, real server-side enforcement, new `LockReason` kind `not_assigned`) and `categorizeForCatalog` (`catalog.ts`, new `CatalogSection` value `hidden`, checked ahead of `comingSoon` so a Coming Soon gated placeholder is invisible too, not shown-with-a-badge): a gated assessment is invisible/blocked while `completionStatus === 'not_started'` and there is no pending assignment or pending reassessment schedule (the latter exempted since a reassessment schedule only ever exists for an assessment the member already has real history with) — never hides a member's own in-progress draft or completed history, same "core protection rule" the framework already had for tier locks. `questionnaireCatalog.ts` skips building a card at all for a `hidden` entry (no wasted per-type query). `/questionnaires`' Assigned section and the Home summary card's underlying catalog both shrink correctly; the Assigned section now shows calm copy ("Nothing here yet. Your coach will assign these when the time is right.") instead of disappearing when nothing is assigned, so a member always knows where a coach assignment will show up.

**Real gap found and closed #1**: `app/assessments/primal-pattern-diet-type/page.tsx` and its `take/page.tsx` had *zero* access enforcement of any kind before this task, not even the pre-existing tier check every other assessment already had (confirmed by reading both files directly) — a member could reach it by direct URL regardless of tier or, now, assignment. Both now call `checkAssessmentAccess` exactly like the generic engine/WBSA routes already did.

**Real gap found and closed #2**: nothing in the codebase ever transitioned `assessment_assignments.status` from `'pending'` to `'completed'` when a member actually finished the assigned questionnaire (confirmed by reading every reference to the table) — without fixing this, a completed assignment would stay in `facts.pendingAssignment` forever, which this task's "moves out of the priority spot once completed" requirement depends on being false. Fixed centrally with one new AFTER INSERT trigger on `assessment_attempts` (migration `00000000000144_questionnaire_assignment_gating.sql`) — since every one of the 5 completion sources (generic engine, Primal Pattern, Onboarding, Body Assessment, Unified Runtime) already converges into that one insert-only ledger via existing triggers (migration 79/100), this closes the gap for all of them at once without touching any of those 5 trigger functions. The same migration also adds a partial unique index (`(member_id, assessment_definition_id) where status = 'pending'`) — DB-level enforcement of "one active assignment per member per questionnaire" — and `assignAssessmentAction` now checks for an existing pending row first (idempotent: a duplicate assign returns success, not an error, and a stray race is caught as a `23505` conflict and treated the same way).

**Home priority placement**: new `components/dashboard/AssignedQuestionnairePriorityCard.tsx`, reading `questionnaireCatalog.assigned` (already-batched, no new query) — a dark forest-green/gold card, the same "From Root" chrome language as the pop-up chain, rendered as the very first thing inside `<main>` on `/dashboard`, above Quick Actions/Today, in both the first-check-in and normal branches. Renders nothing when nothing is assigned (silently disappears, same posture as every other conditional dashboard zone); disappears from this spot automatically once the migration's trigger flips the assignment to completed.

**New pop-up**: `questionnaire_assigned`, added to `RootPopupMessage` (`app/actions/rootPopupMessages.ts`) and checked first in the waterfall (a coach's direct action outranks Root's own day3/day7/offer messages), keyed by the assignment row's own id (`questionnaireAssignedPopupMessageKey`, `lib/root-popup-messages/data.ts`) so a new assignment cycle for the same questionnaire always earns a genuinely new pop-up. Copy exactly as specified: "Something new from your coach" / "Your coach has assigned you the [name] questionnaire. It helps Root understand you more deeply, and your answers go straight to your coach." / "Start now" (routes straight into the questionnaire) / "Not now" (closes only, never touches the assignment or any other message's own dismissal row). Same one-time-ever shape as the existing offer pop-ups (`RootMessagePopupClient.tsx`'s ignore-on-mount effect, extended to this kind).

**Regression tests against the real, documented starvation bug** (fixed 2026-08-02, commit `85bdb347`: one dismissed pop-up used to permanently kill every later one): extracted the waterfall's own "check due-ness, fall through to the next candidate" logic into a small pure helper, `pickFirstDueOneTimeMessage` (`lib/root-popup-messages/data.ts`), used by the new branch for a member's (possibly several) pending assignments, and unit-tested directly (`tests/root-popup-messages.test.ts`): a dismissed earlier candidate falls through to a later still-due one rather than returning null, multiple dismissed candidates in a row still fall through correctly, and null is returned only once every candidate is exhausted, never before.

**Other new tests**: `tests/assessment-registry-catalog.test.ts` (pure, fast) — hidden-by-default, surfaced-once-assigned, never-hides-in-progress, moves-to-completed, self-serve-assessments-never-hidden, coming-soon-gated-placeholders-stay-hidden. Extended `tests/assessment-registry-integration.test.ts` (real local Supabase) with a new "assignment gating — DB-level enforcement" describe block proving the partial unique index rejects a true duplicate pending row, allows a new cycle once the prior one leaves pending, and the trigger really does flip an assignment to completed (and clears `facts.pendingAssignment`) the moment a real completion is inserted. Updated the pre-existing membership-tier-gating tests in that same file (and one in `tests/wbsa-registry.test.ts`) whose old assertions described the now-intentionally-changed behavior — e.g. "membership-tier member: Nutrition & Lifestyle unlocked" is no longer true on tier alone, an assignment is required regardless of tier now.

**Verified**: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npm run lint` — 0 errors, 90 warnings, identical to the pre-existing baseline. Full `npx vitest run` (after a fresh `supabase db reset`, applying migration 144 along with every prior one) — 3607/3608 passing across 316/317 test files; the one failure (`tests/correlation-engine-integration.test.ts`) is the same pre-existing Spearman date-math flake documented throughout this file's history, unrelated to this task. `npm run build` compiled successfully, every route generated including the updated Primal Pattern and generic-engine assessment routes. Em dash guard (`tests/no-em-dash-guard.test.ts`) passes with zero new violations — every new string in this task (pop-up copy, empty-state copy, lock-reason copy) is em-dash-free.

**Two more real, pre-existing bugs found live and fixed** (neither introduced by this task's own new code, both caught only because live verification actually exercised these exact paths for the first time):
1. **A real hydration mismatch on `/questionnaires`** (`lib/assessments/presentation.ts`'s `formatAssessmentDate`): `toLocaleDateString('en-US', {...})` had no explicit `timeZone`, so it resolved against the host process's own local zone — Vercel's server runs in UTC, a member's browser runs wherever they physically are, so the same completed-assessment date could render different text server- vs. client-side (React error 418/423/425, reproduced consistently against `test.member.populated`'s real completed assessments). This codebase already has the identical fix for the coach side (`lib/time/displayDate.ts`'s own header comment describes the exact same bug class) — applied the same `timeZone: 'UTC'` pin here, the member-facing sibling of that fix.
2. **A real name mismatch in the new pop-up**: the pop-up's first draft named a questionnaire from `AssessmentDefinition.displayName` (the registry's own metadata name) — for Short-HAQ that's "Short Health Assessment Questionnaire," but the assessment's own page, the Home priority card, and the `/questionnaires` catalog all already read the generic engine's own content title, "Health Check-In Questionnaire" (`lib/assessments/short-haq/copy.ts`). Root would have announced one name and landed the member on a page titled something else. Fixed by adding `assignmentId` to `CatalogCard` (`questionnaireCatalog.ts`) and having the pop-up source its candidates from `getMyQuestionnaireCatalog()`'s own `assigned` section instead of a separate, simpler registry-only lookup (which was removed) — one title source for every assigned-questionnaire surface, member-facing and pop-up alike. (The coach's own assignment panel still shows the registry name in its own list — a coach-facing-only, lower-priority, pre-existing instance of the same inconsistency, left alone as out of this task's scope, which is Root's copy to the member.)

**Live-site verification** (`app.mefwellness.com`, `test.member.populated@example.test` / `test.coach@example.test` production test accounts, real Playwright browser contexts, zero console/page errors and zero em dashes confirmed on every screen touched):

- **Coach assigns**: assigned Four Doctors, then later Short-HAQ, to the real production test member via the existing `AssessmentAssignmentPanel` on `/coach/clients/[id]` — both landed as real `assessment_assignments` rows.
- **Pop-up + priority spot**: on the member's next real login (no intervening navigation — an early false negative traced back to the verification script itself double-navigating after the login redirect, which let the one-time pop-up's own auto-dismiss-on-mount fire before the script's second, redundant page load could observe it; not an app bug), the pop-up appeared with the correct questionnaire name, "Start now" routed straight into the questionnaire's real overview page, and going back showed it as the top-priority card on Home, above every other section.
- **No repeat, real logout included**: re-checked on the same login (pop-up correctly absent, a *different*, still-genuinely-due CVS day-3 pop-up correctly took its place instead) and again after an actual sign-out via `/profile` and a fresh sign-in — the assignment pop-up never repeated either time, and the priority card was still there.

## Branded "Reset" Entry Animation (2026-08-03)

Five-stage cinematic sequence (Brand Entrance, The Press, gold Activation, Welcome, Enter the App — `components/entry/RootResetEntryAnimation.tsx`, `~3.6s` total, `~1.15s` reduced-motion) plays once per real session-entry — a fresh login or reopening after a 30+ minute background/close gap — using the existing Root Motion System tokens, the approved logo asset unmodified, and the app's own brand colors. Never plays on internal navigation, form/check-in submissions, or public/pre-auth/coach/admin/first-run (`/welcome`, `/onboarding`, `/name`) pages.

**Session-entry rule** (`lib/entry-animation/rule.ts`, pure, unit-tested): a login-triggered play is decided directly by `signIn()` (`app/actions/auth.ts`), which mints a one-shot random token as the `mef_entry_login` cookie's own value; a reopen-triggered play is decided by `middleware.ts`, comparing a refreshed `mef_entry_last_active` cookie against a 30-minute threshold and minting an equivalent token as `mef_entry_play`. `app/layout.tsx` reads whichever cookie is present (login takes priority) and passes it to `components/entry/RootResetEntryGate.tsx`, which compares it against the last token already consumed — tracked in `sessionStorage`, never sent over the network — and only plays when they differ. A separate Page Visibility listener in the same Gate covers the one case the server can't see at all: an already-open tab backgrounded past the threshold and brought back to the foreground, using `app/api/entry-animation/greeting/route.ts` to resolve the member's name at that moment. Logging out clears all three cookies so the next login always replays.

**A real, pre-existing gap fixed along the way**: `signIn()` previously always redirected to `/` and ignored `middleware.ts`'s own `redirectedFrom` query param, so a deep link a signed-out member followed was never actually honored after logging back in. `signIn()` now resolves its real destination in the same request (`lib/auth/postLoginRoute.ts`, shared with `app/page.tsx` so the role/consent/onboarding routing logic isn't duplicated) and redirects there directly — a signed-out visit to `/profile` now correctly lands back on `/profile` after login, not forced to `/dashboard`.

**Three real production-only bugs found and fixed, each only reproducible against a live deployment, not local dev or a local production build**:
1. A cookie `middleware.ts` sets does not reliably reach the browser on the RSC-fetch response Next.js's client router uses to follow a Server Action's `redirect()` — confirmed via raw response capture (no `Set-Cookie` header at all on that specific response, while the identical write on a hard reload worked). Fixed by having `signIn()` set its own token directly instead of asking middleware to mint one for the login trigger.
2. Both entry-token cookies were made non-`httpOnly` (a random token, nothing sensitive) after confirming `app/layout.tsx`'s own server render is inconsistent about seeing the just-set cookie for that same redirect — `RootResetEntryGate.tsx` now cross-checks `document.cookie` directly as the authoritative source, with a short retry (up to 5×150ms) for a residual timing gap between the browser applying the redirect's `Set-Cookie` and the component's first render.
3. The overlay's own tap-to-skip handler (modeled on `components/reveal/RevealSequence.tsx`'s precedent) was removed entirely after confirming it was the actual cause of a near-instant dismissal: the "Log in" button's own tap can land on the newly-mounted full-viewport overlay as a same-position "ghost click" the instant it covers the screen where that button used to be.

**Tests added**: `tests/entry-animation-rule.test.ts` — the session-entry decision (login/gap/excluded-path/public-path branches), the excluded-path matcher, the Stage 4 greeting-copy fallback, and the stage-timing budget (including a regression guard for a real bug found during this build: Exit/finish were originally scheduled as a fixed mount-relative offset that always included the "still waiting for the name" delay even when no wait ever happened, pushing the common case to ~4.4s instead of the intended ~3.6s, over the brief's 4s ceiling — fixed by scheduling Exit/finish relative to when Welcome actually starts).

**Verified**: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npm run lint` (repo root) — 0 errors, same 90 pre-existing warnings. Full `npx vitest run` (after a fresh `supabase db reset`, per this repo's own established Playwright-pollutes-the-DB pattern) — 315/316 test files, 3589/3590 tests passing; the one failure is the same pre-existing `correlation-engine-integration.test.ts` Spearman date-math flake documented throughout this file's history. `npm run build` compiled successfully, all routes generated. Verified locally with Playwright against a real production build (`npm run build && npm run start`, seeded dev account `member.one@example.test`) across many repeated runs: fresh login shows the full sequence with no dashboard flash, internal navigation and hard reloads never replay it, logout→login always replays it, a signed-out deep link to `/profile` correctly lands on `/profile` after login, a simulated 30-minute gap correctly replays on reopen, and reduced motion produces the ~1.15s simplified version — 100% reliable across every local run.

**Live-site verification, an honest limitation**: logged into `app.mefwellness.com` with the standing `memberPopulated` production test account and drove the flow directly with Playwright (mobile viewport), the same way local verification was done. Deep-link preservation verified working correctly on the live site (a signed-out visit to `/profile` correctly returns there after login). The animation itself was **intermittently unreliable on the live site** — in repeated fresh-login test runs, it played correctly (confirmed via full phase-by-phase console logging matching the intended ~3.6s timing) in some runs, and did not visibly appear at all in others, despite the three fixes above each being individually confirmed to resolve a real, reproducible cause when tested in isolation. The remaining intermittency was not fully root-caused before this task ended — it did not reproduce at all in extensive local testing (only ever seen against the live Vercel deployment), and is the one thing in this build that is not yet trustworthy. Flagging this explicitly rather than claiming full live-site success: **do not consider this feature done until someone confirms live reliability directly**, ideally with a larger sample of real logins than this session had time for.

## Progressive Reveal Engine (Prompt 3, 2026-08-02)

Replaced walls of text with paced, conversational reveals on Moment screens per `docs/motion-experience-bible.md`'s new "§13a. Progressive Reveal Engine" section (added by this task, cross-referenced from §14's Prompt 3 row). Applied only to screens the Bible's §2 classification table calls a Moment — no Tool screen (check-in, Food Lens, Protein Ledger, dashboard, exercise library, chat, Progress, settings) was touched.

**Engine built** (`apps/consumer-web-app`):
- `components/reveal/Typewriter.tsx` — the one shared char-by-char typewriter implementation (45ms/char, the same rate `lib/introRevealTiming.ts` already codified), extracted so there's a single implementation instead of two. `components/IntroReveal.tsx` and `app/welcome/WelcomeFlow.tsx`'s Page 2 (Story) — the original hand-rolled version this idiom was proven on — both render it internally now, with no external API change to either.
- `components/reveal/RevealSequence.tsx` — the generic sequenced-reveal engine behind Bible §5's fade → headline → pause → body → pause → action template. Steps are mount-gated (not CSS-hidden), a tap anywhere completes the rest instantly, and `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` (via `lib/motion/useReducedMotion.ts`) skips the whole sequence from the first render with no reveal at all. Also exports `RevealFade`, the skip-aware fade wrapper every step uses.
- `components/reveal/ConversationFlow.tsx` — `RevealSequence` specialized for Bible §6's "Conversational sequence" pattern: an array of short Root messages, each held on screen for its own reading-time floor (`lib/reveal/timing.ts`'s `readingFloorMs`, the wordCount/3-second rule from §5) before the next mounts.
- `components/reveal/StepCard.tsx` — the "multi-step card" pattern: entirely member-paced (tap to advance, never a timer), so nothing needs a separate skip affordance.
- `components/closing-screen/KeyFindingReveal.tsx` — wraps the existing, already-proven `useCloseScreenReveal`/`useDelayedReveal` primitives from `components/closing-screen/ClosingScreenPrimitives.tsx` (built for Core Values Snapshot/Life Signal Check/Readiness Pulse) in a small reusable component, so a Server Component results page can gate a server-rendered finding behind one quiet beat without duplicating the mechanism.
- `lib/reveal/timing.ts` — reading-time pacing math (re-exports `lib/introRevealTiming.ts`'s real constants rather than inventing new ones; adds `readingFloorMs`, the first actual implementation of Bible §5's wordCount/3-second auto-advance floor, previously specified in prose only).
- `lib/reveal/text.ts` — `splitIntoSentences`, the same `.split(/(?<=[.!?])\s+/)` idiom `lib/onboarding/coachCopy.ts` already used, for turning an existing paragraph into paced beats without rewording it.

**Reuse, not duplication** (per this repo's own completion workflow): `components/closing-screen/ClosingScreenPrimitives.tsx`'s staged-reveal mechanics, `lib/motion/useReducedMotion.ts`, `components/motion/Fade.tsx`'s `.mef-fade-in` idiom, and `lib/introRevealTiming.ts`'s 45ms/char rate were all read from and built on top of, never reimplemented.

**Real gap found and closed**: reading `app/assessments/wbsa/results/[sessionId]/page.tsx`, `app/assessments/[questionnaireId]/results/[assessmentId]/page.tsx` (the shared CHEK HLC1 / Four Doctors / Short-HAQ results page), and `app/assessments/primal-pattern-diet-type/results/[assessmentId]/page.tsx` directly confirmed none of the three had any staged-reveal mechanics at all — each rendered its key finding instantly, on every visit, unlike Core Values Snapshot/Life Signal Check/Readiness Pulse's own closing screens. Per this prompt's own requirement 6 ("assessment results and closing screens... are Moments: their key finding should be revealed with anticipation"), each now wraps its actual finding in `KeyFindingReveal`: WBSA's "Areas with more reported patterns"/"fewer concerns"/suggestions block (its safety-flag warning, when present, is deliberately left instant — never delay a safety message), the generic engine's score-ring hero card, and Primal Pattern's `HeroResultCard`. First-time-only per session, instant on every revisit, skipped outright under reduced motion. The finding's own data and wording are unchanged in all three; only when it mounts changed.

**Walls of text converted**: audited every Moment screen (welcome, onboarding, first check-in, Reset Plan, guest wellness-check preview, and all assessment closing screens) for paragraphs over 50 words per Bible §6. Welcome, onboarding, first check-in, and Reset Plan were already clean (onboarding's `ConsentForm.tsx` legal disclosure text is a deliberate, out-of-scope exception — legal copy shouldn't be turned into a narrative reveal). The real violations were three closing-screen paragraphs: `buildCvsClosingReinforcement` (55 words) and `CVS_HANDOFF.body` (54 words) in `components/core-values-snapshot/CvsCloseScreen.tsx`, and `buildLscClosingReinforcement` (56 words) in `components/life-signal-check/LscCloseScreen.tsx`.
