## Core Values Snapshot day-3/day-7 check-ins moved onto the dashboard itself, plus a permanent app-wide em dash ban (2026-08-01)

Two member-testing bug reports handled together.

### Fix 1: Root's day-3/day-7 check-ins were undiscoverable

Bug report: after the Weekly Experiment's day-3/day-7 follow-up "fires," the only way a member could ever see Root's actual question/reflection was tapping "View Result" on the Core Values Snapshot questionnaire card and landing on the standalone `/assessments/core-values-snapshot/experiment` page. The dashboard's own "From Root" carousel tile (`components/dashboard/CoachingMessageCard.tsx`) only ever showed a fixed teaser headline ("Your five-minute experiment") linking out to that page — never the real question text, never an inline answer.

**Fix**: the day-3 question (with its three real answer buttons) and the day-7 reflection (with a new "Got it" acknowledge) now render directly as their own card in the dashboard's "Today" zone, right under Root's Daily Brief — a self-fetching async server component (`components/dashboard/CvsCheckinCard.tsx`, Suspense-wrapped, same "render nothing when there's nothing to say" convention as its carousel neighbors). The actual question/reflection UI was factored out of `CvsExperimentPanel.tsx` into a shared `components/core-values-snapshot/CvsFollowUpCards.tsx` (`CvsDay3FollowUp`, `CvsDay7FollowUp`) so the dashboard card and the standalone experiment page render the exact same real component, not two hand-kept copies. `CoachingMessageCard.tsx` now explicitly renders nothing for the two CVS conversation types (`cvs_day3_checkin`/`cvs_day7_result`) so the same check-in never shows twice on one screen; `getMyCoachingMessage()` still runs and still records the pick into `member_coaching_messages` for that engine's own de-dup bookkeeping.

Day-3 already had a real "answered" signal (`cvs_experiment_daily_logs.day3_response`), so the day-3 card just reads that directly rather than trusting `member_coaching_messages`' "was ever shown" gate (which is a *shown* signal, not an *answered* one — the actual bug: a tile could vanish forever after one render whether or not the member acted on it). Day-7 never had an equivalent, since it was a pure read-only reflection with nothing to submit — added one, migration 135's `lifestyle_experiments.day7_acknowledged_at` (nullable, additive, same shape as migration 134's own `source_session_id` column on that table), set by a new `acknowledgeCvsDay7Action`/`markDay7Acknowledged`. Both cards resolve from real stored state (`day3Response !== null` / `day7AcknowledgedAt !== null`), so answering never leaves a stale duplicate and a page reload correctly makes the card disappear.

Root's day-3 reply is now a real, response-specific reflection (`cvsDay3ReflectionText` in `lib/core-values-snapshot/copy.ts`) shown in place of the question once answered, replacing the old generic "Thanks for the day-3 check-in." line, on both the dashboard card and the standalone experiment page.

The admin cvs-test-tools day-3/day-7 time-shift summary text (`app/actions/coreValuesSnapshotAdmin.ts`) was updated to point at the new location ("should appear as its own 'From Root' card in the Today section") instead of the old, now-inaccurate "From Root tile" reference.

### Fix 2: permanent em dash ban across the entire app and database

New style law: the em dash character (`—`, U+2014) may never appear in text a member or coach can read, anywhere in the product, permanently. Swept in two passes:

**App code** — every `.ts`/`.tsx` file under `app/`, `components/`, and `lib/` (excluding test files) was scanned with the real TypeScript compiler API (visiting `StringLiteral`/template-literal/`JsxText` nodes only, so comments were never touched and never at risk) to find every genuine em dash, then fixed by hand or via six parallel focused passes across ~266 files, ~950 individual em dashes, replacing each with whichever of a period, comma, colon, or parentheses read most naturally for that sentence, in Root's own voice (never a blind delete). A small, explicit, reviewed set of files were deliberately left alone because their only em dashes live inside LLM system/user prompt strings (the model reads these, never the member — each prompt's own `FORBIDDEN_PHRASES`/safety re-check already guards what the member actually sees) or provider-registry metadata not wired to any UI today; that same list is the guard test's allowlist (see below), so it's a reviewed, visible exception, not silent scope-creep.

One real cross-file coupling caught during verification: `lib/corrective-engine/save.ts`'s program-template name generator changed from `` `${programName} — ${session.label}` `` to `` `${programName}: ${session.label}` ``, but `DraftReviewPanel.tsx`'s `sessionLabelOf()` parsed that exact name back out with a `/— (Session [A-Z])$/` regex — fixed to `/: (Session [A-Z])$/` so session labels still resolve correctly on the coach corrective-program review screen.

**Database content** — migrations 97 (onboarding adaptive question bank), 109 (driver check-in question bank), 76 (Holistic Reset phase labels), 134 (Core Values Snapshot's own question/answer-option/section-subtitle text), 52/53 (proactive-coaching notification `descriptionTemplate`s), and 20 (`assign_client_to_coach`'s conflict error message) all had real em-dash copy in their own `insert`/`raise exception` statements — fixed in the migration files themselves (for a correct historical record and a clean `supabase db reset`), plus a new migration `00000000000136_em_dash_content_cleanup.sql` with real `update`s against each row's own stable natural key (`question_key`, `phase_key`, `rule_key`, etc. — never a bulk regex pass) so already-seeded production rows get fixed too, and a `create or replace function` for `assign_client_to_coach` with the corrected message. `supabase/seed/*.sql` (never run against production per `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`, confirmed by migration 052's own header comment) was fixed too, for local-dev/test consistency, including the ~40-line MEF Knowledge Library content seed. Left alone: `ai_agents.description`/`ai_rules.description` — confirmed by grep to be internal registry metadata never read by any UI component, not member/coach-facing.

Verified the database sweep was actually complete, not just "the files I remembered": queried every `text`/`varchar`/`jsonb` column across all 811 public-schema columns for the em dash character after a fresh `supabase db reset` (migrations 135/136 included) — zero hits outside the two confirmed-internal `description` columns above.

**Guard**: new `apps/consumer-web-app/tests/no-em-dash-guard.test.ts` — same TypeScript-compiler-API technique as the sweep itself (so it inspects real string/template/JSX-text content, never comments), walks `app/`/`components/`/`lib/` on every test run, and fails with exact `file:line` for any future em dash outside the small reviewed allowlist. This is a real, permanent, self-enforcing rule, not a one-time cleanup — the next accidental em dash anywhere in the app fails the test suite.

### Verified

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean (after adding the new `day7AcknowledgedAt` field to three test fixture builders that construct a full `LifestyleExperiment` object). `npm run lint` (repo root) — 0 errors, same 90-warning baseline. Full `npm test` after a fresh `supabase db reset` (migrations through 136 applied clean) — 300/301 test files, 3318/3319 tests passing; the one failure is the same pre-existing `correlation-engine-integration.test.ts` date-math flake documented throughout this doc, confirmed unrelated. Six test files needed their own expected-copy strings updated to match the new (correct, em-dash-free) source text they assert against (`case-view-emptyState`, `food-lens-page-redesign`, `proactive-coaching-scenarios`, `root-map-member-copy`) — logic unchanged, only the literal expected string. `npm run build --workspace=@mef/consumer-web-app` — compiled successfully.

**Verified locally with Playwright** (dev server + local Supabase, real seeded `member.one@example.test`, 390×844 mobile viewport): inserted a real completed Core Values Snapshot session + a real `lifestyle_experiments` row 3 days back (mirroring exactly what the admin time-shift tool itself writes), loaded `/dashboard`, and confirmed a real "From Root" card sits directly in the Today zone (not the carousel, not behind a tap-through) showing the actual day-3 question text and all three real answer buttons. Tapped "Going well" — the card replaced itself in place with Root's real going-well reflection text, no page reload, no duplicate card. Reloaded the dashboard — the card was gone entirely (real `day3_response` now set). Zero console errors throughout. Test fixture rows deleted afterward. Day-7's "Got it" path was verified by code review, the shared-component reuse with the day-3 path, and a clean typecheck/build, but not separately driven in a browser this session — worth a manual check (see report).

**Migrations**: `00000000000135_cvs_day7_acknowledged.sql` (additive nullable column) and `00000000000136_em_dash_content_cleanup.sql` (data-only `update`s + one function redefinition, no schema change). Both applied clean locally via `supabase db reset`; not yet applied to production as of writing this entry (see deploy step below for how that was handled).

**Not verified**: the logged-in experience on the live production URL itself, and the day-7 acknowledge flow specifically — only the local dev server was driven in a browser, per the standing rule not to claim live-site verification that wasn't actually done.

**Deployed**: pushed to `origin/main` (commit `cfe05db`). Vercel auto-triggered a new Production deployment (`mef-platform-e9cc5zjuh-mef-wellness.vercel.app`) for the `mef-platform` project, built successfully, went Ready, target `production`, aliased to `app.mefwellness.com` (confirmed via `vercel inspect`). **Database migrations 135/136 were not applied to production as part of this deploy** — same standing block as every prior production-DB write in this doc (Claude Code's auto-mode safety classifier refuses a direct production DB connection even with a supplied password), so the exact SQL for both was handed to the site owner to run themselves in the Supabase SQL Editor, same pattern as the earlier admin-grant entry above. Until that SQL is run: the dashboard-card fix (Fix 1) itself is fully live immediately (day-3's `day3_response` column already existed in production before this session), but the day-7 "Got it" button will show a graceful "Could not save that" inline error rather than crashing (the new `day7_acknowledged_at` column won't exist yet), and the specific database-seeded copy (onboarding questions, driver check-in questions, Holistic Reset phase labels, the Core Values Snapshot question bank's own prompts/options, two proactive-coaching notification templates, one coach-assignment error message) will keep showing its old em-dash text in production until migration 136 runs — every other em dash in the app (the large majority of member/coach-facing copy) is fixed by this same deploy.


## Root's day-3/day-7 messages now pop up on login instead of only sitting as a card (2026-08-01)

Feature request: nobody was reliably seeing Root's day-3/day-7 Weekly Experiment check-ins even after the previous fix put them on the dashboard itself (2026-08-01, "Core Values Snapshot day-3/day-7 check-ins moved onto the dashboard") — a card in the middle of a long scroll is still easy to miss. Wanted a pop-up right after login that feels like Root greeting the member, with an escape hatch for people in a rush, and a guarantee that a message is never truly lost.

### What was classified as a pop-up message vs. ambient content

Audited every "From Root" surface on the dashboard (`components/dashboard/CoachingMessageCard.tsx`'s conversation types, the Daily Brief/`MorningBriefCard`, `WhatWereNoticingCard`, `RootMapCard`, `RecommendationsCard`) for a real answer/acknowledge affordance, not just observational text. Only two qualified: the Core Values Snapshot day-3 check-in (three real answer buttons) and day-7 reflection (a real "Got it" acknowledge) — both already interactive, both already promised explicitly by Root's own onboarding copy. Everything else (the Daily Brief, and every other Root Coaching Conversation Engine conversation type — `conflicting_information`, `worsening_trend`, `improving_trend`, `repeated_signal`, `first_observation`, `experiment_follow_up`, `reassessment`, `new_assessment_available`) is read-only text with no response affordance, so it stays exactly where it already lives (Today zone / carousel), untouched.

### What was built

**New table** (`supabase/migrations/00000000000137_root_message_popup.sql`): `member_root_popup_dismissals` (`member_id`, `message_key`, `status` in `('snoozed', 'ignored')`, `snoozed_at`), RLS scoped to the owning member. Generalized by a stable `message_key` string (`cvs_day3:<experimentId>` / `cvs_day7:<experimentId>`, see `lib/root-popup-messages/data.ts`) rather than a foreign key into any one feature's tables, so a future Root message of the same shape (real answer/acknowledge, not just an observation) only needs a new case in `app/actions/rootPopupMessages.ts`, not a new dismissal/eligibility system.

**"Maybe later" vs "Ignore" semantics**: "Maybe later" snoozes and must return on the member's *next real login* — implemented by comparing `snoozed_at` against `auth.users.last_sign_in_at` (a real Supabase Auth field GoTrue updates only on an actual sign-in, never a silent token refresh), so a member who keeps the app open all day doesn't get re-interrupted, but a fresh login does bring it back. "Ignore" is permanent (`status = 'ignored'`, never checked against login time again). Both leave the message as an ordinary card; answering/acknowledging (in the pop-up or on the card, both call the same `submitCvsDay3ResponseAction`/`acknowledgeCvsDay7Action`) deletes the dismissal row so nothing lingers.

**Shared "which message is due" logic**: extracted `resolveCvsCheckinPending()` (`lib/core-values-snapshot/experiment.ts`) from what was previously inlined only in `CvsCheckinCard.tsx`, now used by both the card and the new pop-up eligibility check (`app/actions/rootPopupMessages.ts`) so "day 3 before day 7, oldest unhandled first" is computed exactly one way.

**The pop-up itself** (`components/dashboard/RootMessagePopupClient.tsx`): a dark-green, warm modal (forest `#1B3A2D` panel, gold `#C4A050` accents, cream body text — the same Core Values Snapshot design tokens, not a new palette) reusing the exact same copy functions and server actions as the on-page card, so answering inside the pop-up is the same real system as answering on the card, not a second hand-kept copy. No backdrop-click or Escape dismissal on purpose — the only ways out are answering it or one of the two labeled buttons. `router.refresh()` after every action (answer, Maybe later, Ignore) re-fetches the page's Server Components — including `CvsCheckinCard`'s own independent fetch — so the on-page card picks up the new state (gone once answered, badged once snoozed) without a full page reload.

**Never stacks with the wearable welcome modal** (`components/dashboard/HomeScreenPopups.tsx`): both modals are now arbitrated by one client component that freezes "did Root win the pop-up slot" in state on first render. This mattered because `router.refresh()` (fired by answering/snoozing/ignoring) recomputes `app/dashboard/page.tsx`'s server-side eligibility, which would otherwise flip the wearable modal from "suppressed" to "eligible" the instant Root's pop-up closes — i.e. exactly the stacking this was supposed to prevent. Freezing the decision at first mount (ignoring later prop updates) stops that; the wearable modal genuinely waits for a later visit, not just later in the same visit.

**Never fires during onboarding**: gated behind the dashboard's existing `hasCheckins` check (same gate `WearableWelcomeModal` already used) and the `firstCheckin=1` transition param — a brand-new member never has a Core Values Snapshot experiment yet regardless, so this is belt-and-suspenders.

**High-priority badge**: `CvsDay3FollowUp`/`CvsDay7FollowUp` (`components/core-values-snapshot/CvsFollowUpCards.tsx`) gained an optional `isHighPriority` prop — a small gold "Waiting on you" pill next to the "From Root" kicker, shown only once a member has tapped "Maybe later," using the same amber accent token as the app's other highlight UI (`WearableWelcomeModal`'s icon background).

No em dashes were introduced anywhere in the new member-facing copy or UI strings (verified by the existing `tests/no-em-dash-guard.test.ts`, which scans real string/template/JSX-text nodes across `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`).

### Verified

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npm run lint` (repo root) — 0 errors, same 90-warning baseline. Full `npm test` after a fresh `supabase db reset` (migration 137 applied clean) — 301/302 test files, 3329/3330 tests passing; the one failure is the same pre-existing `correlation-engine-integration.test.ts` date-math flake documented throughout this doc, confirmed unrelated. One existing test (`tests/wearable-welcome-modal-timing.test.ts`) needed its "modal is gated behind `hasCheckins`" assertion updated to match the new `HomeScreenPopups`-mediated render (same guarantee, expressed differently — logic unchanged). New `tests/root-popup-messages.test.ts` covers `resolveCvsCheckinPending` (day 3 before day 7, both-resolved, neither-eligible) and `isRootPopupDueThisLogin` (never dismissed, ignored-forever, snoozed-same-login, snoozed-then-real-login). `npm run build --workspace=@mef/consumer-web-app` compiled successfully.

**Verified locally with Playwright** (dev server + local Supabase, real `member.one@example.test`/`member.two@example.test` sessions, 390×844 mobile viewport, real `lifestyle_experiments` rows inserted/backdated directly to mirror what the admin cvs-test-tools time-shift writes): logged in with a day-3-eligible experiment, confirmed the dark-green pop-up rendered with the real question and all three real answer buttons; tapped "Going well," confirmed Root's real reflection replaced the question in place inside the pop-up; tapped "Done," reloaded, confirmed the pop-up and the on-page card were both gone permanently. Repeated for day 7 ("Got it" acknowledges, disappears everywhere). Separately: tapped "Maybe later," confirmed the pop-up closed, the on-page card gained the real "Waiting on you" badge, a plain reload did *not* bring the pop-up back (same login), and a genuine new login (cleared cookies, logged in again) did bring it back. Separately: tapped "Ignore," confirmed the card stayed (no badge) and the pop-up never returned even after a genuine new login. Confirmed `member.two@example.test` (zero check-ins, real seed account) never reaches `/dashboard` at all (routed to `/onboarding`), so the pop-up is structurally impossible for a brand-new member. Confirmed the wearable welcome modal never appeared in the same visit after Root's pop-up closed, even waited 6 seconds past its own 4-second fallback timer and past a manual scroll trigger. Zero console errors throughout. All seeded test data (`lifestyle_experiments`, `member_root_popup_dismissals`) cleared after.

**Verified against production test accounts, live on `app.mefwellness.com`** (after the code deploy below, migration not yet applied — see note): logged in as `test.member.populated@example.test` (fully active) — dashboard loaded cleanly, zero console errors, zero 5xx responses, wearable welcome modal rendered normally (this account has no Core Values Snapshot experiment, so no Root pop-up was expected — correctly absent). `test.member.empty@example.test` (brand-new) never reaches `/dashboard` at all (routed to `/welcome`). `test.member.belowthreshold@example.test` (just started) never reaches `/dashboard` either (routed mid-onboarding, step 8 of 9). **Not verified live**: the pop-up actually firing in production, since none of the three seeded test accounts has a pending Core Values Snapshot day-3/day-7 message today — that path was verified locally instead (above). The graceful-degradation behavior (dismissal queries against the not-yet-migrated production table fail closed, logged server-side, never surfaced to the member) was confirmed by code review of `lib/root-popup-messages/data.ts`'s `try`-free `if (error) return null/false` pattern and by the zero-console-error, zero-5xx live check above.

**Migration**: `00000000000137_root_message_popup.sql` (new table + RLS only, no changes to existing tables). Applied clean to local Supabase via `supabase db reset`. **Not yet applied to production** — this session had no production database credentials (`--db-url` requires the Settings → Database password, which was never supplied this session, consistent with this doc's standing rule that a coding agent doesn't get direct production database write access). Until it's applied, "Maybe later"/"Ignore" will no-op silently (the pop-up still shows and can still be answered normally; the snooze/ignore choice just won't persist yet) — see the report for the exact SQL to run.

**Deployed**: pushed to `origin/main` (commit `2f494ce`). Vercel auto-triggered a new Production deployment (`dpl_EHqwsECs1HKvvvhLxQf4xaSUXkL6`) for the `mef-platform` project, built successfully, went Ready, target `production`, and is aliased to `app.mefwellness.com` (confirmed via `vercel inspect` and a live `curl -I` against the domain). Not verified: the pop-up's answer/snooze/ignore flows on the live production URL itself (see above) — only the local dev server was driven through those specific interactions, per the standing rule not to claim live-site verification that wasn't actually done.


## Fix: Core Values Snapshot interpretation copy claimed a "last two weeks" question that was never asked (2026-08-01)

Bug report from real phone testing on `app.mefwellness.com`: on the "Here's What Root Learned" screen, Root's copy said "when I asked about your last two weeks, Peace & Calm got a 2 out of 5" — a claim that Root had asked a specific question naming a two-week window.

### What the attention question actually asks

Checked the real Screen 2 content (`supabase/migrations/00000000000134_core_values_snapshot.sql`, rendered by `ScaleBattery` in `components/core-values-snapshot/CvsQuestionCards.tsx`). Each of the six attention sliders (`cvs_q5`-`cvs_q10`) only ever shows a short label at the moment the member rates it: "Your body and energy," "The people closest to you," "Fun and play," and so on, on a 1-5 scale ("None at all" to "Real, protected time"). None of the six individual questions says "the last two weeks." That exact phrase appears exactly once: in a section-level intro sentence (`CVS_SCREEN2_INTRO`) shown above all six sliders together, on the same screen, before the member starts rating them ("For each of these, be honest about the last two weeks. Not your intentions. Your calendar."). So Root's later claim, worded as "when I asked about your last two weeks, X got a Y," attributes a specific, repeated question to something that was actually said once, as a general framing instruction, not per question.

### Diagnosis, all four branches plus one related observation

Checked all four "Here's What Root Learned" branches (`buildWhatRootLearned` in `lib/core-values-snapshot/copy.ts`) for this exact claim shape: Clear Gap ("when I asked about your last two weeks, X got a Y out of 5") and Aligned ("when I asked about your actual last two weeks? You're living it: Y out of 5") both had it. Split doesn't reference the attention rating at all (it's built entirely from the Q1-Q4/Q11 "what matters" answers), and Slipping already only said "you gave it a Y out of 5" with no timeframe claim, so both were already accurate. Also checked every other place that reads `scoring.attention`: the S1 guilt-area "surprise" observation (`buildS1Observation`, fires when the Q3 guilt area's own attention rating is 4 or higher) had the identical claim ("your last two weeks say you're actually showing up for it"); `buildKeyInsightCopy`, `buildGapVisualCopy`, and the persisted "What Root Knows So Far" narrative draft (`narrative.ts`) all already said "attention it's getting" with no timeframe claim, so none needed a change.

### Fix

Per the task's guidance (fix Root's copy to match what was actually asked, note here rather than change the question if the question should change instead): kept the fix on Root's copy, not the question. Root's own instruction to the member (`CVS_SCREEN2_INTRO`, "be honest about the last two weeks") already reads clearly and doesn't need a per-question restatement — six sliders each individually saying "in the last two weeks, how much attention has X gotten" would be repetitive on a single screen the member is already reading top to bottom. Rewrote the three affected lines to describe only the mechanism actually used, a 1-5 attention rating, not an invented specific-timeframe question:
- **Clear Gap**: "when I asked about your last two weeks" → "when I asked how much attention it's actually been getting."
- **Aligned**: "when I asked about your actual last two weeks?" → "when I asked how much attention it's actually getting?"
- **S1 (guilt-area surprise)**: "your last two weeks say you're actually showing up for it" → "the attention you said you're actually giving it says you're showing up for it."

No em dashes in any of the new copy (verified by the existing `tests/no-em-dash-guard.test.ts`).

### Guard tests

New `describe` block in `tests/core-values-snapshot-copy.test.ts` (3 new tests): Clear Gap and Aligned both confirmed to never contain the old "last two weeks" phrasing and to contain the new attention-scoped wording plus the real `att` value; the S1 observation confirmed the same. All existing tests in that file (Split/Clear Gap/Aligned/Slipping/narrative accuracy guards from the earlier 2026-08-01 em-dash-day fix) still pass unmodified.

### Verified

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npm run lint` (repo root) — 0 errors, same 90-warning baseline. Full `npm test` after a fresh `supabase db reset` — 301/302 test files, 3332/3333 tests passing; the one failure is the same pre-existing `correlation-engine-integration.test.ts` date-math flake documented throughout this doc, confirmed unrelated (this was a pure `core-values-snapshot` copy change). `npm run build --workspace=@mef/consumer-web-app` compiled successfully.

**Not driven in a browser this session** — this is a pure copy/logic fix to a pre-existing screen, verified via unit tests against real constructed answer sets for each affected branch, not a UI change. No new screens or interactions were added.

**No migration, no database content changed** — this was purely a change to the copy-generation function; the underlying question text, scoring, and stored data are all untouched, so there is nothing to run in the Supabase SQL Editor for this fix.

## Life Signal Check — Experience 2 of the free arc (2026-08-01)

Second free-tier "conversation with Root," built exactly on Core Values Snapshot's own template and quality standard: same Unified Adaptive Assessment Foundation/Runtime, same registry pattern, same seven-beat flow shape (intro → screens → What Root Learned → Weekly Experiment offer → educational resource → close), same "What Root Knows So Far" card mechanics, same day-3/day-7 follow-up system now delivered through the existing Root pop-up modal (2026-08-01, "Root's day-3/day-7 messages now pop up on login"). No new engines: this experience reuses the runtime, `lifestyle_experiments`, `cvs_experiment_daily_logs`, the Member Health Narrative system, the Root Coaching Conversation Engine, and the pop-up dismissal system as-is, with two small, additive generalizations described below. Unlocks only after Core Values Snapshot completes.

### Content — 11 questions, 3 screens (migration 138)

Screen 1 ("The Wide Lens," `cvs_q1`-parallel `lsc_q1`-`lsc_q3`): best/hardest time of day (natural order, not randomized) and "if your body could send you one text" (6 options, randomized — same `seededShuffle` Core Values Snapshot's own Q1-Q4 use, imported directly rather than reimplemented).

Screen 2 ("Six Signals," `lsc_q4`-`lsc_q9`): one question per signal (energy, sleep, tension, digestion, body, mind), each its own single-select screen (not a slider battery like Core Values Snapshot's Screen 2, since each question's own option text differs signal to signal). Each answer scores 0-3; every signal's four options score 0/1/2/3 evenly except Tension, whose five options score 0/2/2/2/3 per the build brief exactly (`lib/life-signal-check/constants.ts`'s `SIGNAL_OPTION_SCORES`, keyed per-question rather than assumed from option index anywhere else in the codebase).

Screen 3 ("The Call," `lsc_q10`-`lsc_q11`): Question 10's options are generated live from the Screen 2 answers, same dynamic-option pattern as Core Values Snapshot's own Q12 (`lib/life-signal-check/q10.ts`) — shows only "loud" signals (score ≥ 2) with the "which would you pick to quiet" framing; if nothing is loud, flips to "which would you most want to protect" and shows all six. Question 11 (duration: just this week / a few weeks / months / as long as they can remember) sets the tone of Root's interpretation.

### Scoring and the four patterns (`lib/life-signal-check/scoring.ts`)

- **One Loud Signal** — exactly 1 or 2 signals score ≥ 2 (a single clear leader, even when a second signal is also elevated).
- **A Chorus** — 3 or more loud signals; Root names the Question 10 pick as the starting thread and names the others honestly.
- **Quiet Body** — nothing scores ≥ 2; Root gives an honest "nothing came in loud" observation rather than manufacturing a finding.
- **Body-Value Echo** — a conditional overlay (not a fifth mutually-exclusive branch, same shape as Core Values Snapshot's own S1 guilt observation layering on top of its four branches): fires only when the *loudest* signal is adjacent to the member's Core Values Snapshot top value **and** that value's branch is `clear_gap` or `slipping` (a real gap — never fires on `aligned`, since there's nothing to echo). The adjacency mapping (`lib/life-signal-check/adjacency.ts`), explicit and documented in code:
  - Health & Energy → Energy, Body
  - Close Relationships → Tension
  - Growth & Learning → Mind
  - Purpose & Meaningful Work → Energy
  - Freedom & Play → Mind
  - Peace & Calm → Mind, Tension (the build brief's own worked example)
  
  Sleep and Digestion are deliberately never adjacent to any Core Values Snapshot value — no forced mapping exists, so Echo simply can't fire for those two loudest signals, which is honest rather than a gap to fill.

The **surprise beat** fires only when Question 3 was answered "I'm okay, actually" **and** at least one Screen 2 signal scored ≥ 2 — Root's exact line from the build brief about the gap between self-summary and what showed up.

**Pick-wins rule**: Question 10's answer always becomes the member's `chosenSignal` for every downstream screen (What Root Learned, the Weekly Experiment, the loudness visual's gold bar), even when a different signal scored higher. When they diverge, Root says so honestly (verbatim per the brief): "You picked X even though Y scored louder. You know things the numbers don't."

### Copy (`lib/life-signal-check/copy.ts`)

Every sentence is scoped to exactly what `scoring.ts` checked, following the same accuracy discipline Core Values Snapshot's own copy module documents (a real overclaim bug there, fixed 2026-08-01, is the reason this module never invents a timeframe or repetition claim that wasn't actually asked). Question 11's answer sets tone: curiosity for "just this week," respect and patience — never alarm — for "as long as they can remember." No causation claims anywhere. Zero em dashes (verified by the existing `tests/no-em-dash-guard.test.ts`, which scans this new module along with everything else under `lib/`).

**Six Weekly Experiment theories, one per signal** (`buildLscExperimentTheoryCopy`), each a real 5-minute daily action, timed to the member's own "hardest time of day" answer where that's natural:
- **Energy**: a genuine 5-minute break at the hardest point in the day, no phone, no task.
- **Sleep**: 5 screen-free minutes before bed, a clear "day is done" signal.
- **Tension**: 5 minutes at the hardest point in the day to physically release held tension (shoulders, jaw), not a stretch routine.
- **Digestion**: the first 5 minutes of one meal a day, eaten without doing anything else at the same time.
- **Body**: 5 minutes of gentle movement matched to what makes the ache feel more manageable.
- **Mind**: 5 minutes at the hardest point in the day doing absolutely nothing on purpose — not scrolling, not "relaxing productively."

Day-3/day-7 follow-up question/reflection text (`lscDay3FollowUpText`/`lscDay3ReflectionText`) reads identically to Core Values Snapshot's own (both were already fully generic, parametrized only by the experiment's own label, never Core-Values-Snapshot-specific in wording) — reused directly rather than duplicated. Day-7's closing bridge line differs by design ("you've now named what matters and heard what's loudest... one more conversation left") and has its own `lscDay7FollowUpText`.

### Two small, additive generalizations (no new engines)

1. **`lifestyle_experiments.source_experience_key`** (migration 138, nullable, additive) — the previous "which experience started this" signal was `recommendation_id is null`, which could no longer distinguish a Core Values Snapshot experiment from a Life Signal Check one once a second such experience existed. Existing Core Values Snapshot-sourced rows are backfilled to `'core-values-snapshot'` in the same migration statement (safe, since no Life Signal Check experiment could exist anywhere this migration runs); `startCvsExperimentAction` and the new `startLscExperimentAction` both set it going forward. `lib/core-values-snapshot/dailyLogsData.ts`'s `findLatestCvsExperiment` was fixed to filter on this real key instead of the old heuristic.
2. **Root Coaching Conversation Engine candidates** — `lib/life-signal-check/coachingCandidates.ts` mirrors `lib/core-values-snapshot/coachingCandidates.ts` exactly; `app/actions/rootCoaching.ts`'s `gatherAndPlan` now splits a member's experiments three ways (Recommendation Engine-sourced, Core Values Snapshot-sourced, Life Signal Check-sourced) instead of two, and `selectCoachingCandidates`/`planCoachingConversation` gained an additive `lscCandidates` field alongside the existing `cvsCandidates` one. Two new `ConversationType` values (`lsc_day3_checkin`, `lsc_day7_result`) added to the existing vocabulary (migration 138, same drop/re-add pattern as every prior addition to this constraint) and to `templates.ts`/`questions.ts`'s exhaustive `Record<ConversationType, ...>` maps (both experiences' day-3/day-7 candidates always carry a final `precomposedMessage` and skip these template builders in practice — they exist only so those maps stay total).

`cvs_experiment_daily_logs` (migration 134) is reused as-is for Life Signal Check's own daily taps/day-3 response — its schema was never actually Core Values Snapshot-specific, only its table name, and it's keyed purely by `experiment_id`. No new table.

### Root's pop-up modal and follow-up cards — real bug found and fixed during this build

`app/actions/rootPopupMessages.ts` now checks Core Values Snapshot before Life Signal Check (oldest experience first) for which day-3/day-7 message is due, one at a time — the loser simply waits as its own dashboard card. `RootMessagePopupClient.tsx` and `CvsFollowUpCards.tsx` (the shared `CvsDay3FollowUp`/`CvsDay7FollowUp` components, now also reused by `LscCheckinCard.tsx` and `LscExperimentPanel.tsx`) dispatch which server action and which experience's copy to use per message.

**Real bug caught by this session's own browser verification, not by typecheck or tests**: the first version passed each experience's copy *functions* (`lscDay7FollowUpText`, etc.) as props from `LscCheckinCard.tsx` — a Server Component — into the Client Component follow-up cards. This compiled and typechecked cleanly but crashed at runtime ("Functions cannot be passed directly to Client Components unless you explicitly expose it by marking it with 'use server'") — only Server Actions (not ordinary functions) can cross that boundary as props. Confirmed live in the dev server log during Playwright verification (the day-7 pop-up was silently falling back to Core Values Snapshot's own bridge line for a Life Signal Check message). Fixed by replacing the function props with a plain, serializable `experience: 'core-values-snapshot' | 'life-signal-check'` string prop; `CvsFollowUpCards.tsx` resolves the real copy functions from that string internally, inside the Client Component. `onSubmit`/`onAcknowledge` props were never affected — real Server Actions (from a `'use server'` file) are specifically supported crossing that boundary, unlike plain functions.

### Registry, gating, and the prerequisite mechanism (first real use)

`lib/assessment-registry/types.ts` already had a `prerequisites.prerequisiteKeys: AssessmentKey[]` field and `status.ts`'s `calculateLockReason` already had real logic to check it — but every existing entry set it to `[]`, and both call sites (`access.ts`'s `checkAssessmentAccess`, `catalog.ts`'s `categorizeForCatalog`) always passed `new Set()` for `completedPrerequisiteKeys`, so the mechanism was fully wired but never exercised. Life Signal Check's registry entry (`lib/assessment-registry/registry.ts`) sets `prerequisiteKeys: ['core-values-snapshot']` — the first assessment to actually use this field — which required fixing both call sites to compute a real completed-keys set from the same batched `getMemberAssessmentFacts` query they already run, rather than adding any new query or a bespoke gating path. `app/actions/questionnaireCatalog.ts`'s card-building loop was updated the same way. The Life Signal Check overview page (`app/assessments/life-signal-check/page.tsx`) renders the real `describeLockReason` message with a link back to Core Values Snapshot when locked — no new copy path, the same generic lock-reason renderer every other gated assessment already uses.

Because Life Signal Check uses `storageAdapter: 'unified-assessment-runtime-tables'` (same as Core Values Snapshot and WBSA), it was automatically picked up by `questionnaireCatalog.ts`'s existing generic unified-runtime branch (the same one a 2026-07-31 fix repaired for Core Values Snapshot/WBSA) — no new per-assessment catalog branch needed.

`lib/investigation-engine/registry.ts` and the `AssessmentKey`/`ConversationType`/`ResultAdapterId`/`StorageAdapterId` unions were extended additively; three existing tests with hardcoded registry-entry counts/lists (`assessment-registry-integration.test.ts`, `investigation-engine.test.ts`) were updated to include the 11th entry — logic unchanged, only the expected counts/lists.

### Core Values Snapshot's own handoff, finally real

The "Start the Life Signal Check" button on Core Values Snapshot's own closing screen (`components/core-values-snapshot/CvsResultsView.tsx`) was a permanently disabled "Coming soon" placeholder since that experience shipped (2026-07-31) — now a real, enabled button routing to `/assessments/life-signal-check`. `getClientCvsSessionDetailAction`'s `continuedToExperience2` field (shown on the coach's Core Values Snapshot detail page) went from a hardcoded `false` to a real check (`hasStartedLscAction`) of whether the member has any Life Signal Check session at all.

### "What Root Knows So Far" — now cumulative across experiences

`components/core-values-snapshot/WhatRootKnowsCard.tsx` gained an optional `notes` array (default `['core-values-snapshot']`, unchanged existing behavior for Core Values Snapshot's own page). Life Signal Check's results page passes `['core-values-snapshot', 'life-signal-check']` so the card grows to include both experiences' entries rather than only its own — matched by note alone (not scoped to a single session id) when more than one note is requested, since every narrative write here already dedupes to one active row per category+title, so "by note" always resolves to the member's current understanding, not stale history. A real, matching bug in this same logic (the id-scoping was originally left on unconditionally, so Core Values Snapshot's entries silently never appeared on Life Signal Check's results page) was caught and fixed during this session's own Playwright verification, not by any automated check.

### Coach view

`/coach/clients/[id]/life-signal-check/[sessionId]` — all six signal scores (ranked, loudest and chosen flagged), the pattern that fired, whether the pick diverged from the top score, the duration answer, whether Body-Value Echo/the surprise beat fired, and Weekly Experiment status/streak/day-3 response — same shape as Core Values Snapshot's own coach detail page. `LifeSignalCheckPanel.tsx` (summary list + link, same shape as `CoreValuesSnapshotPanel.tsx`) wired into the client detail page alongside it.

New `tests/life-signal-check-scoring.test.ts` (33 tests): each of the four patterns constructed and proven to fire only under its own real condition (including the boundary between "one loud" and "a chorus" at exactly 2 vs. 3 loud signals); the surprise beat proven to require both its conditions independently (never fires on either alone); the Body-Value Echo adjacency mapping proven reachable for every value area that has one (a real loop over `VALUE_ADJACENT_SIGNALS`, not a single hand-picked case) and proven to never fire on the `aligned` branch or with no Core Values Snapshot context at all; Question 10's option-filtering proven both ways (loud-only "quiet" framing vs. all-six "protect" framing); the pick-wins rule proven with a real diverging case; copy-accuracy tests confirming the honest "pick diverged" line only appears when it should and is absent on the `quiet_body` pattern; narrative-draft tests confirming the Echo/surprise entries are never invented when their conditions didn't fire.

## Life Signal Check refinements (bug fix, cap UX, accuracy fix, nav, intro standard, design fixes) — 2026-08-01

Nine-part refinement pass on Experience 2, triggered by a real bug the user hit on their own live account. No new migration — every fix is application code reusing columns/tables migration 138 already created.

### 1. The real bug: the active-experiment cap was counting real, orphaned rows the member could never see

Root cause (found by investigation, not guessed): `components/dashboard/RecommendationsCard.tsx` — the dashboard's *only* link to `/recommendations` (the sole screen that lists Recommendation-Engine-sourced `lifestyle_experiments` and lets a member close them) disappears the moment its underlying recommendation is marked `completed`, which `startMyExperiment` does automatically the instant an experiment starts. So starting an experiment from a recommendation, then never revisiting `/recommendations` before its tile vanished, leaves the `lifestyle_experiments` row `active` forever with **zero navigational path back to it** — it just sits there occupying one of the two cap slots. `lib/lifestyle-experiments/data.ts`'s `countActiveExperiments` was already correctly excluding overdue rows via `deriveEffectiveStatus`, so the miscount was never a scoring bug — it was real, uncounted, unreachable rows.

Compounding bug found in the same investigation: `resetCvsForMemberAction` (`app/actions/coreValuesSnapshotAdmin.ts`) deleted `lifestyle_experiments` by `recommendation_id is null`, a heuristic that also matches Life Signal Check's own rows now that a second `recommendation_id`-null experience exists — a Core Values Snapshot admin reset could silently delete a member's Life Signal Check experiment too. Fixed to filter on `source_experience_key = 'core-values-snapshot'` (migration 138's own real disambiguator) instead. New regression test in `tests/core-values-snapshot-admin-integration.test.ts` seeds a real Life Signal Check experiment alongside the Core Values Snapshot one being reset and proves it survives.

Fix, `lib/lifestyle-experiments/data.ts`: new `expireOverdueExperiments(supabase, memberId)` actually **persists** the "past day 7, no reflection" verdict (`isExperimentOverdue`) back onto the row's `status` column, instead of only ever recomputing it in memory at read time — called at the top of both `countActiveExperiments` and `listMyLifestyleExperiments`, so any overdue row self-heals to `expired_no_reflection` for real, in the database, the moment anyone next reads it. No cron needed. This is the literal "past day 7 close out automatically" the user asked for. New tests in `tests/lifestyle-experiments-active-cap.test.ts` prove a real DB row flips status on read, and that a still-current row is never touched.

The user's own live account had two such stray rows sitting invisibly at the cap — closing them out (or waiting seven days for the new auto-expiry to clear old ones) is the one-time cleanup needed; see the report for the exact click path, no SQL required.

### 2. Cap flow UX — real, in-place recovery, not just a better error message

`components/life-signal-check/LscExperimentPanel.tsx`'s offer screen now calls the existing `getMyLifestyleExperiments()` (already used by `/recommendations`) to check the real cap live, client-side. At cap: the "I'm in: start the 7 days" button gets `disabled` + `aria-disabled="true"` and a muted, clearly-not-tappable style (no more looking clickable while silently failing), and every currently active experiment — regardless of source (Recommendation Engine, Core Values Snapshot, or Life Signal Check) — is listed right there with a real "Close this out" (reflection + `reflectAndCloseMyExperiment`) or "Stop early" (`abandonMyExperiment`) action, reusing the exact same server actions `/recommendations`' own close flow already uses. Closing one updates local state immediately; the start button re-enables and the member can start the new experiment without leaving the screen or the taker flow. This same panel is what the dashboard now shows too (see #3), so a member blocked at the cap always has a real way out, wherever they hit it.

### 3. Accuracy fix: the closing screen no longer claims a running experiment that doesn't exist

Real bug: `LSC_CLOSING_REINFORCEMENT` was a single unconditional line claiming "it's already an experiment running to prove something real" — shown even to a member blocked by the cap or who simply declined to start. `lib/life-signal-check/copy.ts`'s `buildLscClosingReinforcement(didStartExperiment: boolean)` now branches for real; `LifeSignalCheckTaker.tsx` computes `didStartExperiment` from whether the member's current Life Signal Check experiment (`onStatusChange` now bubbles `LscExperimentPanel`'s own live status up to the taker) is actually tied to *this* session (`sourceSessionId === sessionId`), not just "does one exist at all."

Dashboard "start it later" path: `getMyLscOfferAction` (new, `app/actions/lifeSignalCheck.ts`) finds the member's latest completed Life Signal Check session when no experiment exists yet for it; `LscCheckinCard.tsx` renders the real `LscExperimentPanel` offer screen (theory, button, and — if they're still at cap — the same inline close-out list from #2) instead of disappearing, so a member who was blocked or declined never loses the conversation's payoff.

### 4. Navigation — a persistent way back to the dashboard mid-flow

New shared `components/ExperienceHomeLink.tsx` — a labelled "Home" pill (same visual language as the Check-In wizard's own Home button, chosen deliberately over an icon-only glyph per that component's own documented reasoning: a word label is more reliably tappable). Rendered on Life Signal Check's interpretation, experiment, resource, and closing screens (`LifeSignalCheckTaker.tsx`) — previously the only way out of those screens was the in-flow Continue button or the phone's back button. Every answer in these takers already persists per-question as it's given, so unlike the check-in wizard this needs no "save progress" step, just a direct `router.push('/dashboard')`. Applied to Core Values Snapshot's identical taker too for consistency (same gap existed there, not explicitly asked for the CVS side but left inconsistent would violate "consistent with the rest of the app").

### 5. New permanent design standard: progressive-reveal intros

New `components/IntroReveal.tsx` — headline fades in first, then each body line reveals on its own delay (reusing the app's existing `.mef-fade-in` keyframe + `animationDelay` staggering idiom, the same one `CheckinForm.tsx`/`WelcomeFlow.tsx` already use elsewhere — no new animation vocabulary). Reduced motion is handled entirely by `.mef-fade-in`'s own pre-existing `prefers-reduced-motion` override (`animation: none !important`), which already renders every line instantly and fully visible — no separate JS detection needed. Purely presentational (no card, no button), so it drops into whatever container a screen already uses.

Applied to Core Values Snapshot's and Life Signal Check's own intro screens (`CVS_INTRO_COPY`/`LSC_INTRO_COPY` in their respective `copy.ts`), the two named in the request, with copy tightened to roughly half its previous length (3 sentences → 2 short lines each), same voice and hook. Audited every other intro/welcome screen in the app (`OnboardingIntro.tsx`, `FirstCheckInWelcome.tsx`, `app/welcome/WelcomeFlow.tsx`'s cinematic Story page, the body-assessment/food-lens camera-instruction intros) and made a deliberate scoping call: Welcome Flow's Story page already implements an equivalent (more elaborate, typewriter-based) headline-then-body reveal with its own reduced-motion fallback — reusing this component there would be a downgrade, not an improvement. Onboarding's expectations screen and the first-check-in card already use short, single-sentence copy with their own bespoke staggered per-block entrance — not the "long static paragraph, no reveal" problem this component solves. Left those as-is; happy to extend `IntroReveal` to them too if wanted. This is now the component every future experience should reach for.

### 6. Em dash sweep

No em dashes found in any Life Signal Check member-facing content (questions, copy, resource piece, day-3/day-7 text) — `tests/no-em-dash-guard.test.ts` already exists (added in the 2026-08-01 Core Values Snapshot cleanup) and scans every real string/template/JSX text node under `app/`, `components/`, `lib/` with the TypeScript compiler API, not a plain grep, so it catches what a human skim would miss. It already passed before this session's changes and still passes after every new string this session added.

### 7. Design-session fixes, all in `lib/life-signal-check/` (scoring.ts, copy.ts, constants.ts, q10.ts) + `LifeSignalCheckTaker.tsx`

- **a. Question 1 contrast insight** — new `scoring.ts` field `q1ContrastFires` (true only when Q1 and Q2 name two different, specific times of day — never fires on "not much of the day"/"varies"), rendered as its own callout box in `WhatRootLearnedSection`, styled like "You feel most like yourself in the mornings, but by evening it's gone."
- **b. Question 2 wired explicitly into experiment timing** — `timingPhrase()` in `copy.ts` now says so out loud: "...since that's when you said it gets loudest," not just an implicit "hardest point in the day."
- **c. Question 3 generalized surprise beat** — new `BODY_TEXT_SIGNAL_GUESS` map (constants.ts) maps each of Q3's five real body-text answers to the signal it predicts; `scoring.ts`'s `q3Comparison` ('confirmed' | 'mismatch' | null, null on `quiet_body` since there's no genuine "loudest" to compare against a field of zeros) drives copy's honest, both-directions line: "You called this in the first question. Your body predicted itself." or "Earlier you said: I'm tired. Three screens later, it's actually Mind." The existing "I'm okay, actually" surprise beat is untouched — this generalizes it to the other five answers, not a replacement.
- **d. Body-Value Echo is an overlay, never competes with the base pattern** — `buildLscEchoLine(scoring)` now names the real loudest signal: "Your loudest signal is X, and it happens to sit right next to what you told us matters most," always rendered as its own box alongside (never instead of) whichever base pattern fired.
- **e/f. Question 10/11 branching**, `LifeSignalCheckTaker.tsx`: exactly one loud signal skips Question 10 entirely (auto-records it, shows "This is the one that's been loudest: Energy" instead of a pick with no real choice) and goes straight to Question 11; on the Quiet Body branch (nothing loud), Question 11's prompt is rephrased live to "How long has this felt this good?" and its own duration copy (`durationLineQuietBody`) never says a signal is "showing up" or "speaking up."
- **g. Six Signals question order shuffled per session** — `seededShuffle(SCREEN2_QUESTION_KEYS, sessionId:...)`, same technique and same primacy-bias reasoning as Core Values Snapshot's own shuffle. Resume logic (`determineInitialBeat`) uses the same shuffled order so a reload lands on the right question.
- **h. Question 11's tone now genuinely differentiated across all four duration answers** — the build brief and this module's own header comment only ever named two poles (curiosity / patience); `durationLine()` now gives "a few weeks" and "months" their own distinct registers (measured attentiveness, respect) too, and the header comment documents all four.
- **i. Coach view shows the member's raw Q1-Q3 answers** — new "What they actually said (Q1-Q3)" section on `/coach/clients/[id]/life-signal-check/[sessionId]`, reading straight from the session's own stored answers via new `TIME_OF_DAY_RAW_LABEL`/`BODY_TEXT_LABEL` maps (the real on-screen option text, distinct from the sentence-embeddable phrases used elsewhere), alongside the existing derived scores/pattern.

### Bug found and fixed during this session's own browser verification

While driving the at-cap scenario, the browser console showed a real React warning: "Cannot update a component (`LifeSignalCheckTaker`) while rendering a different component (`LscExperimentPanel`)." Caused by calling the new `onStatusChange` prop *inside* `setStatus`'s state-updater function (which can run during React's render phase). Fixed by moving it into its own `useEffect` keyed on `status`. Confirmed clean (zero console errors) on a second full run afterward.

## Follow-up: same accuracy fix extended to Core Values Snapshot, intro reveal extended to onboarding and first-check-in — 2026-08-01

Requested immediately after the above: Core Values Snapshot had the identical "closing screen always claims a running experiment" bug as Life Signal Check (same code shape, never explicitly asked for in the original request, flagged as an FYI in that session's report). Fixed the same way.

- `lib/core-values-snapshot/copy.ts`: `CVS_CLOSING_REINFORCEMENT` (a static string) replaced with `buildCvsClosingReinforcement(didStartExperiment: boolean)`, same two-branch shape as Life Signal Check's own fix.
- `components/core-values-snapshot/CvsExperimentPanel.tsx`: new optional `onStatusChange` prop, bubbled via its own `useEffect` (not inside the state updater — avoids the exact React warning caught and fixed in Life Signal Check's panel).
- `components/core-values-snapshot/CoreValuesSnapshotTaker.tsx`: computes `didStartExperiment` from whether the member's current experiment is tied to *this* session, passes it to `CloseSection`.
- New `getMyCvsOfferAction` (`app/actions/coreValuesSnapshot.ts`), mirroring `getMyLscOfferAction` exactly. `components/dashboard/CvsCheckinCard.tsx` now renders the real `CvsExperimentPanel` offer screen instead of disappearing when the member has no current experiment.

Also extended the new progressive-reveal intro standard to the two screens flagged as candidates in the prior report:

- `app/onboarding/OnboardingIntro.tsx` — its eyebrow/title/purpose block now uses `IntroReveal` (purpose split into its natural two sentences), with `titleTag="h1"` since this headline is genuinely this page's main heading (no other h1 exists on this screen, unlike Core Values Snapshot/Life Signal Check's takers which already have their own sr-only h1 elsewhere). The journey card, time caption, and CTA button's own existing staggered entrance delays were pushed back to start only once the reveal finishes.
- `components/FirstCheckInWelcome.tsx` — its one-paragraph body split into its natural two sentences and run through `IntroReveal`; the CTA link and caption below now fade in after.

**Real bug found and fixed during this session's own browser verification**: `FirstCheckInWelcome.tsx` is a Server Component (no `'use client'`), but calling `introRevealFollowUpDelayMs` — imported from `components/IntroReveal.tsx`, a Client Component — at module scope threw `introRevealFollowUpDelayMs is not a function` at runtime. Next.js treats every export of a `'use client'` file as a client reference once any Server Component imports it, even a plain, non-React helper function; it silently fails when actually called server-side rather than erroring at build/typecheck time. Fixed by extracting the pure delay math into a new `lib/introRevealTiming.ts` (no `'use client'` directive), which `IntroReveal.tsx` now also consumes for its own defaults. All four call sites (`OnboardingIntro.tsx`, `FirstCheckInWelcome.tsx`, and both takers) now import `introRevealFollowUpDelayMs` from the new pure module instead of from the component file.

## Em dash sweep of stored database content, plus a one-time "start it later" pop-up (2026-08-01)

Two member-testing bug reports handled together.

### Fix 1: em dashes still visible in the live app despite the earlier "permanent ban" sweep

The user found real em dashes in two places: an old Weekly Experiment card's stored text ("deliberately small — this isn't about") and dashboard coaching text ("your last check-in — today is about easing back in"). Both looked exactly like already-fixed source strings in `lib/core-values-snapshot/copy.ts` and `lib/brain/copy.ts` — because they are. The earlier sweep (2026-08-01, "permanent app-wide em dash ban") fixed every *template*; it did not and could not retroactively fix rows that were already written to the database by the *old* version of those templates before that fix was deployed. Confirmed by re-querying every one of the 820 public-schema `text`/`varchar`/`jsonb` columns on a fresh `supabase db reset` (all migrations through 138 applied): zero em dashes anywhere except the two already-known-internal `ai_agents.description`/`ai_rules.description` columns — so the code-level guard (`tests/no-em-dash-guard.test.ts`, which already scans all of `app/`, `components/`, `lib/` under `apps/consumer-web-app`, the monorepo's entire text-generating surface — `apps/*` has no sibling app, and `packages/`/`services/` are empty stubs per this doc's own "Not Built" section) has no gap. This was purely stale historical production data, not a remaining code problem.

**Found four tables where the app composes real prose once, at experiment/recommendation/message/narrative-write time, and freezes the result into a row that's never regenerated** — so any row written before the code fix keeps showing the old text forever:
- `lifestyle_experiments.title`/`.protocol` — frozen at experiment-start time from `buildExperimentTheoryCopy`/`buildLscExperimentTheoryCopy` (`app/actions/coreValuesSnapshot.ts`, `app/actions/lifeSignalCheck.ts`). This is the "old experiment card."
- `member_recommendations.title`/`.explanation`/`.why_this_was_selected` — composed entirely by `lib/recommendation-engine/{builder,describeForMember}.ts`, never edited by a member or coach. This is the "dashboard coaching recommendation text."
- `member_coaching_messages.message_text` — per that table's own migration 96 header comment, "composed entirely from already-approved template copy."
- `narrative_items.title`/`.summary` ("What Root Knows So Far") — but *only* for the provenance values the engine itself writes (`system_observed`, `inferred`, `confirmed_recurring`). `member_reported`/`coach_entered` rows are a real member's or coach's own typed words, found via `app/actions/narrative.ts`'s `addCoachNarrativeItemAction`/`correctNarrativeItemAction`, and are deliberately excluded — this is someone's own writing, not app copy, and not this fix's business to rewrite.

Also deliberately excluded: `lifestyle_experiments.reflection_text` (the member's own written reflection).

**Fix**: `supabase/migrations/00000000000139_em_dash_stored_content_sweep.sql`. Unlike the earlier migration 136 (a small, enumerable set of seed rows fixed by hand, one `update ... where question_key = '...'` per row), this data is one row per real member action — there's no natural key to match by hand. Instead, a small local `fix_em_dash_temp()` SQL function (created, used, and dropped again within this same migration — not a permanent schema addition) turns every em dash into "period, capitalize the next word" — the exact shape every real example in the app used (`" — this isn't"` → `". This isn't"`), matching how the original sweep resolved these same templates by hand, applied only to `update ... where col like '%—%'` rows so it's a no-op everywhere else. Verified directly against real inserted-then-rolled-back rows in all four tables, including one `coach_entered` narrative row with a deliberate em dash confirmed to survive untouched.

### Fix 2: the "start it later" offer now pops up once too

Feature request: the day-3/day-7 pop-up (shipped earlier today) covers the mid-experiment check-ins, but a member who completes Core Values Snapshot or Life Signal Check and doesn't start the Weekly Experiment right then only ever sees the offer again if they scroll to the dashboard card themselves. Wanted a one-time pop-up on the next login, Root's voice, the theory in one line, and a button to start or dismiss to the card — same pop-up system as day 3/day 7.

Reused every piece of that system exactly as it already exists, added two new message kinds (`cvs_offer`/`lsc_offer`) alongside the existing four:
- **`app/actions/rootPopupMessages.ts`**: `findMyPendingRootPopupMessage()` now also checks `getMyCvsOfferAction()`/`getMyLscOfferAction()` (the same actions `CvsCheckinCard.tsx`/`LscCheckinCard.tsx` already call) whenever there's no current experiment for that experience. Priority order unchanged in spirit: Core Values Snapshot before Life Signal Check, and within each, day 3 before day 7 before that experience's own offer (day 3/7 and the offer can never both be pending for the same experience at once, since the offer only exists when no experiment is running).
- **One-time semantics, genuinely different from day3/day7**: day3/day7 keep returning on every login until answered or explicitly "Ignore"d. The offer must show *at most once, ever*. New `isOfferPopupDue()` (`lib/root-popup-messages/data.ts`) — due iff no dismissal row exists at all, full stop, no snooze/next-login case. `RootMessagePopupClient.tsx` writes that dismissal (reusing the exact same `ignoreRootPopupMessageAction` the day3/7 "Ignore" button already calls, `member_root_popup_dismissals`, no new table) the instant the offer mounts, not only on an explicit click — so even a member who closes the tab without touching it never sees it a second time. The dashboard card (`CvsCheckinCard.tsx`/`LscCheckinCard.tsx`, both **completely unchanged**, per the ask) stays the permanent, un-timed way to start it later either way.
- **The pop-up itself**: a new `RootOfferPopup` sub-component in the same file, same dark-green/gold Root design tokens as the day3/7 modal. Shows the real one-line theory (`buildExperimentTheoryCopy`/`buildLscExperimentTheoryCopy`'s `.theory` field, e.g. "My theory: your energy runs out because your day has scheduled output but never a scheduled recovery.") and the same "I'm in: start the 7 days" button `CvsExperimentPanel`/`LscExperimentPanel` already use, calling the same `startCvsExperimentAction`/`startLscExperimentAction` — starting from the pop-up is the same real system as starting from the card, not a second hand-kept copy. A real cap error (member already at the two-active-experiment limit) surfaces the exact same error text the card's own action already returns; the full close-out flow for that case stays on the card (Life Signal Check's own), not duplicated in the pop-up. "Not now" just closes — the dismissal was already recorded on mount.
- New `lib/root-popup-messages/data.ts` unit tests for `isOfferPopupDue` (due once, never again regardless of dismissal status, and — unlike `isRootPopupDueThisLogin` — never revived by a later login) plus `cvsPopupMessageKey`/`lscPopupMessageKey`'s new `'offer'` kind.

### Verified

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npm run lint` (repo root) — 0 errors, same 90-warning baseline. Full `npm test` after a fresh `supabase db reset` (migration 139 applied clean, a no-op on fresh data as expected) — 302/303 test files, 3392/3393 tests passing; the one failure is the same pre-existing `correlation-engine-integration.test.ts` date-math flake documented throughout this doc, confirmed unrelated. `npm run build --workspace=@mef/consumer-web-app` compiled successfully, `/dashboard` and every other route generated.

**Verified locally with Playwright** (dev server + local Supabase, real `member.one@example.test`/`member.two@example.test`, 390×844 mobile viewport, zero console errors throughout every run): seeded a real completed Core Values Snapshot session with no experiment yet (via the service-role client, same technique as the existing admin test tools), loaded `/dashboard`, confirmed the real one-time pop-up appeared with the real one-line theory and the real "I'm in: start the 7 days" button. Scenario A: tapped "Not now," confirmed the pop-up closed, reloaded the dashboard, confirmed the pop-up did **not** reappear while the on-page card still offered to start it (unchanged). Scenario B: seeded a fresh session, tapped the real "I'm in: start the 7 days" button inside the pop-up, confirmed a real `lifestyle_experiments` row was created (`status: 'active'`, correct `source_session_id`) via a direct service-role query, and confirmed the pop-up closed. Separately repeated the same seed-and-start flow for Life Signal Check (real member, six real Six-Signals answers forcing a real "Energy" loudest signal), confirmed the real Life-Signal-Check-specific theory line rendered ("your energy runs out because..."), tapped start, and confirmed a real `lifestyle_experiments` row with `source_experience_key: 'life-signal-check'` was created. All seeded sessions/answers/experiments/dismissal rows deleted afterward via the service-role client; confirmed zero residue with a final count query before finishing.

**Migration**: `supabase/migrations/00000000000139_em_dash_stored_content_sweep.sql` (data-only `update`s against four tables, via a function created and dropped within the same migration — no schema change, no new table). Applied clean locally via `supabase db reset`. **Not yet applied to production** — same standing block as every prior production-database write in this doc (no production database credentials available to this session). The exact SQL to run is the migration file itself — see the report for the ready-to-paste version.
