## Life Signal Check refinements round 2: five reported bugs, Active Experiments dashboard section, closing screen redesign (2026-08-01)

Full end-to-end pass on user-reported bugs plus a permanent design principle ("luxury editorial experience, not a software application") applied to Life Signal Check's closing screen. No em dashes anywhere (verified by the existing `tests/no-em-dash-guard.test.ts`, which scans every new string this session added).

### Bug 1: the em dash sweep (migration 139) missed two more frozen-at-write tables

Root cause, found by tracing `MorningBriefCard.tsx`'s `brief.coaching_recommendation` back through `lib/coaching-engine/service.ts`'s `getOrCreateTodaysMorningBrief`: `coach_morning_briefs` (migration 53) is "idempotent per (member, local_date) ... a permanent snapshot ... never recomputed retroactively" — the exact same freeze-at-write-time shape as the four tables migration 139 already fixed, just not enumerated there. `lib/brain/copy.ts`'s `buildReasonText` template was already fixed (period, not em dash) — but a brief generated before that fix deployed keeps showing the old text for that entire `local_date` forever, since old dates are never revisited. `coaching_insights` (migration 66) has the identical shape and was missed for the same reason.

**Fix**: `supabase/migrations/00000000000140_em_dash_morning_brief_and_insights_sweep.sql` — same `fix_em_dash_temp()` local-function-created-and-dropped pattern as migration 139, applied to every text column on both tables (all system-composed, never a member's or coach's own words). Applied clean locally via `supabase db reset`. **Not yet applied to production** — no production database credentials available to this session, same standing block as every prior production-database write in this doc. Ready-to-paste SQL is the migration file itself; given to the user directly in this session's report.

### Bug 2: "start it later" offer never appeared for a member with any prior experiment history

Root cause: `getMyCvsExperimentStatusAction`/`getMyLscExperimentStatusAction` (`findLatestCvsExperiment`/`findLatestLscExperiment`) return the member's most recently-created experiment for that experience regardless of status — active, completed, abandoned, or expired. Once a member has ever had a single experiment for an experience, that query keeps returning it forever, even long after it wrapped up. `CvsCheckinCard.tsx`/`LscCheckinCard.tsx` (dashboard) and `rootPopupMessages.ts`'s `findMyPendingRootPopupMessage` both treated "status exists" as "an offer can never be relevant," so a member who declined a *newer* completed session — after any earlier experiment, from any source, had ever finished — saw neither the dashboard card nor the one-time pop-up. This matches the exact reported symptom.

**Fix**: both the dashboard card logic (now consolidated into `ActiveExperimentsSection.tsx`, see below) and `findMyPendingRootPopupMessage` now only treat a still-`'active'` experiment as blocking the offer; a terminal one falls through to the real offer check. Verified live locally: declined Life Signal Check via plain Continue (member.one already had prior experiment history from earlier testing), reloaded `/dashboard` with no re-login, and the real offer card and pop-up both appeared immediately, with the dashboard coaching text rendering with no em dash.

### Bug 3: experiment lifecycle drift (duplicate CVS experiments, cap list disagreeing with reality)

No single reproducible root cause found without production database access (standing block, as above) — the account state described (`closed two duplicate Peace & Calm experiments... cap screen later listed Tension and Peace & Calm, Sleep missing`) can't be reconstructed from code alone. What *was* found and fixed: **no guard previously existed against starting a second active experiment for the same experience** — `startCvsExperimentAction`/`startLscExperimentAction` only enforced the total-across-everything cap (`MAX_ACTIVE_EXPERIMENTS`), never "is there already an active one for *this* experience." A double-tap, two open tabs, or the new offer pop-up and the dashboard card both firing could each independently create a duplicate "Peace & Calm" row. Both actions now refuse with a clear message ("You already have an active ... experiment. Close it out first.") if the member's latest experiment for that same experience is still active.

A read-only diagnostic query (every `lifestyle_experiments` row for the user's own account, oldest first) and the migration 140 SQL are both included in this session's report for the user to run themselves and share back if the drift recurs — this session has no production credentials to inspect or reconcile the real account directly.

### Bug 4: single-loud-signal Question 10 skip

Already correct in code from the prior refinement session (`LifeSignalCheckTaker.tsx`'s `singleLoudSignal` branch, screen3Index 0) — verified again by the existing 44-test `life-signal-check-scoring.test.ts` suite (still passing) and by a real local Playwright run reaching the "This is the one that's been loudest" statement screen. No change needed.

### Bug 5: "Later, remind me" did nothing but navigate to the dashboard

`onLater` was always just `router.push('/dashboard')` — identical to the "Return to Dashboard" button directly below it — with no reminder system behind it at all. Per Root's accuracy rule (never promise what the app can't deliver), building a real reminder system for a not-yet-built third experience was out of scope; the honest fix is copy: `LSC_HANDOFF.secondaryButton` is now "Not now, back to dashboard," which is exactly what it does.

### Active Experiments dashboard section (item 6)

New `components/dashboard/ActiveExperimentsSection.tsx` replaces the two per-experience dashboard cards (`CvsCheckinCard.tsx`/`LscCheckinCard.tsx`, deleted — both only ever rendered when a day-3/day-7 follow-up was due, never on an ordinary day 2 or day 5). `CvsExperimentPanel`/`LscExperimentPanel` already rendered exactly what item 6 asked for (day progress, the real daily question, a done-for-today state, day-3/day-7 when due) once given a real, active status — both panels' `sessionId`/`topValue`/`chosenSignal` props became optional (only needed for the not-yet-started branch) so the dashboard section can render them directly from an already-active status without a second fetch. Recommendation-Engine-sourced active experiments (no daily-tap mechanism of their own) get an honest name+progress+"log or close this out" row instead of an invented question. Section renders nothing at all (not even its own heading) when there is truly nothing to show.

### Daily question rewrite (item 7)

`lscDailyPromptCopy` changed from `(signalLabelText: string)` to `(signal: Signal)`, naming the real action per the build brief: Energy → "your protected break," Sleep → "your five screen-free minutes before bed," Tension → "your physical release," Digestion → "those first five undistracted minutes," Body → "your five minutes of gentle movement," Mind → "your five minutes of doing nothing on purpose." Pure function of the signal, so an already-active experiment gets the new question immediately, not only future ones. New `SIGNAL_BY_LABEL` reverse lookup (constants.ts) recovers the real `Signal` from a stored experiment's `title` (which is always exactly `SIGNAL_LABEL[signal]`) wherever only the title is available.

### Typewriter IntroReveal (item 8)

Full rebuild of `components/IntroReveal.tsx`: the headline now visibly types itself out letter by letter (45ms/character, reusing the exact idiom already proven on `app/welcome/WelcomeFlow.tsx`'s own Page 2 typewriter — `.mef-typewriter-caret`, not a new animation vocabulary), then body lines flow in one at a time, then an optional caller-owned `button` prop arrives last. New "play once per screen" rule: a `storageKey` prop gates a localStorage flag so a member who has already seen a given intro screen gets the final state instantly on every later visit; `prefers-reduced-motion` always gets the instant result. A real race was caught and fixed during this session's own reasoning (not live-tested, since it only matters cross-component): the "mark as seen" write is deliberately delayed until the reveal actually finishes, not written immediately on mount, so a sibling `IntroRevealFollowUp` component (new — the Server Component half of this contract, since `OnboardingIntro.tsx`'s/`FirstCheckInWelcome.tsx`'s own follow-on content can't hold client state or receive a callback across that boundary) can never read a same-visit write before it has captured its own "first time" reading. `lib/introRevealTiming.ts`'s `introRevealFollowUpDelayMs` signature changed to `(title, lineCount)` to account for the headline's own now-variable typing duration; all four call sites updated. Verified live locally: a screenshot taken mid-animation shows the Life Signal Check intro headline cut off mid-word ("Where is your lif"), confirming it visibly plays, not just fades in all at once (the exact bug reported).

### Vertical centering (item 9)

Applied `flex min-h-[60vh] flex-col justify-center` to both experiences' intro, "What Root Learned," Weekly Experiment, and resource beats (`LifeSignalCheckTaker.tsx`, `CoreValuesSnapshotTaker.tsx`) — the single-card screens the user specifically named. A full app-wide audit of every member screen was not attempted given the size of the app (84+ routes) and the real risk of wrongly centering a genuinely long, scrolling page (a form, a coach panel); any other screen the user notices this on is a quick, low-risk follow-up fix once named.

### Closing screen redesign (items 10-18)

Scoped to Life Signal Check's own closing screen (`LifeSignalCheckTaker.tsx`'s `close` beat) — the one the user tested and described (Readiness Pulse, Body-Value Echo, "Conversation 2 of 3"). Core Values Snapshot's parallel closing screen is structurally identical and untouched; a good candidate for the same treatment if wanted.

New `components/life-signal-check/LscCloseScreen.tsx` replaces the old `CloseSection` (removed from `LscResultsView.tsx`) plus the inline raw title/summary narrative list:

- **Celebration + filling progress line (items 10, 15)**: one integrated visual, not two — a horizontal line between three conversation nodes; on first view only, the segment up to "Life Signal Check" fills in, its checkmark draws itself along its own SVG path (new `.mef-close-check-draw`/`.mef-close-check-circle` keyframes, distinct from the existing `.mef-capture-check` scale-pop), a single one-shot soft gold sweep crosses it (new `.mef-close-gold-sweep`, distinct from the existing infinite-loop `.mef-scan-sweep`), and "Conversation 2 of 3" lands a beat later. An `sr-only` list carries the same three conversations' full descriptive labels for assistive tech, since the visual line is `aria-hidden`. Reduced motion and any revisit render the final, settled state instantly.
- **Structured insight cards (item 11)**: `InsightCard` matches a narrative item's own stable title (not a stored flag) to decide how to render it — the real loudness bars (`LoudnessVisual`, reused as-is, gold for the chosen signal) for "How your body is responding" instead of a sentence with digits; everything else falls through to a plain label+finding card.
- **Body-Value Echo diagram (item 12)**: new `buildLscEchoDiagram` (copy.ts) plus a new `echoContext: CvsContextForEcho | null` field on `LscScoring` (only ever set when `echoFires`) — a simple three-node vertical diagram (top value → current pressure → loudest signal, gold for the last node) replaces the prose `buildLscEchoLine` on this one screen (that function itself is untouched, still used for the stored narrative-item summary and the "What Root Learned" screen's own callout).
- **Next-chapter framing (item 13)**: both Life Signal Check's and Core Values Snapshot's "I don't know yet" narrative drafts (`lib/life-signal-check/narrative.ts`, `lib/core-values-snapshot/narrative.ts`) rewritten to "That's exactly what our next conversation finds out." `InsightCard` also matches on title (`"What's behind"` / `"What's pressing on"`) to render this framing for any narrative item already written before this change, not only future ones — no data migration needed for this particular fix.
- **Root Observation card (item 14)**: new `buildLscRootObservation` (copy.ts), one honest line scoped to exactly what this session's own scoring found, revealed via the same `IntroReveal` typewriter every intro screen now uses (reuse, not a second animation system) — gated to only mount once its own card is actually visible (a real timing bug caught and fixed during this session: a naively-nested `IntroReveal` would otherwise finish typing invisibly while its parent card was still mid fade-in).

## Readiness Pulse — Experience 3, the free arc's final conversation (2026-08-02)

Built the third and last free-tier conversation per a fully locked design brief: nine questions across three screens (Honest History, Capacity Not Motivation, The Decision), a derived readiness formula whose thresholds are documented below, her own Question 9 pick always overriding the derived read (same precedence rule as Life Signal Check's Question 10), four readiness patterns each with a distinct experiment, an Evidence Echo overlay, a Question 8 vs. Life Signal Check comparison with graceful degradation, a direct write into the existing coaching-style profile, and a six-beat closing screen in a deliberately different order than Life Signal Check's/Core Values Snapshot's own. No new engines: built entirely on the existing Unified Adaptive Assessment Runtime, Lifestyle Experiments table, `cvs_experiment_daily_logs`, the Root pop-up system, and `narrative_items`.

### The derived readiness formula (documented thresholds)

Capacity score = Q4 (genuinely_open=3, room_if_protect=2, small_pockets=1, almost_none=0) + Q7 (easily_doable=3, doable_good_days=2, sounds_small_know_myself=1, even_that_heavy=0), range 0-6. Willingness score = Q3 (overdue=3, curious=2, appealing_but_exhausting=1, a_little_scary=1) + 1 for having answered Q8, range 1-4 (always 2-4 once the session is actually complete, since Q8 is required). Willingness bands directly off that score (<=2 low, ==3 medium, ==4 high — Q3's own three distinct values plus the constant +1 already produce exactly three clean bands). Capacity bands: Q7==0 or capacityScore<=2 is thin (an explicit override for "even that feels heavy," per the brief's own parenthetical), capacityScore>=5 is strong, everything else medium. Full 3x3 pattern table (`lib/readiness-pulse/scoring.ts`'s `deriveReadinessPattern`): willingness low → not_yet regardless of capacity; willingness medium + capacity thin → ready_if_small; willingness medium + capacity medium/strong → still_deciding; willingness high + capacity strong → ready_now; willingness high + capacity thin/medium → ready_if_small. Q6 (the obstacle) is never scored, only stored. Her Q9 pick always wins as `finalPattern` for every downstream decision (experiment, copy, coach view); `derivedPattern` is retained only so Root can honestly name a divergence.

### Question 5 → the coaching style profile (single source of truth, no competing store)

Question 5's hypothetical ("what would you want from me if two days slipped") maps onto four coaching styles, only one of which (`direct`) already existed in `wellness_coaching_style_profile.tone_preference`. **The one genuine architectural conflict found during this build**: forcing the other three onto an existing value would have meant Root claiming something untrue about what the member actually said. Resolved the way most faithful to the brief's own "single, living profile" instruction: migration 141 additively extends the enum (`meaning_anchored`, `adaptive`, `autonomous` alongside the existing four), `lib/intelligence-core/coachingStyle.ts`'s deterministic keyword classifier gets matching keyword lists for all three (so any *future* coaching_preferences narrative text using this language keeps recomputing the same tone, not only this one-time write), and `lib/readiness-pulse/coachingStyleWrite.ts` writes an immediate, explicit `upsertCoachingStyleProfile` call at confidence 0.9 — bypassing the generic sample-size confidence formula on purpose, since fed only one new data point it would land near 0.45, below the 0.5 floor the coach prompt requires before using a style at all, and the brief is explicit that a direct member statement becomes "the current coaching preference at high confidence" immediately, not eventually. Every other dimension (detail/task-load/time-commitment) carries forward unchanged from whatever was already on the profile. A matching `coaching_preferences` narrative row is also written (`member_visible: false`) so the same real evidence feeds any future recompute. `lib/intelligence-core/service.ts`'s `coachingStyleGuidanceText` gained real guidance lines for the three new tones so Root's replies actually reflect the answer, not silently ignore it. A real keyword collision was found and fixed during local testing: `EDUCATION_KEYWORDS`' generic bare `'why'` matched Readiness Pulse's own "remind me why I started" text, tying with `meaning_anchored` and losing the tie-break — fixed by dropping the redundant bare `'why'` (still fully covered by `'explain'`/`'understand'`).

### Evidence Echo, Q8 comparison, readiness level storage

Evidence Echo (`getEvidenceEchoContext` in `app/actions/readinessPulse.ts`) fires only when the member's Life Signal Check experiment is active or completed with at least one real daily log within the last 14 days, floored at the experiment's own start date (a real bug caught and fixed during local verification: without that floor, a data anomaly could produce a nonsensical "4 of the last 1 days" claim — unreachable in real usage since logging always stamps today's date, but the floor makes the numbers self-consistent under any condition, never just "usually right"). Question 8 vs. Life Signal Check's own loudest signal: confirms, gives an honest mismatch, or simply doesn't fire (no manufactured comparison) when Life Signal Check found nothing genuinely loud (`quiet_body`) or doesn't exist. Readiness level and the biggest obstacle (Q6) are stored per the brief's "invisible to the member, visible to the coach" requirement as `narrative_items` rows with `member_visible: false` — a real, RLS-enforced boundary (`member_read_own_narrative` requires `member_visible = true`), not just a UI filter, and readable for free by every existing narrative_items consumer (coach client view, the coaching-style classifier, any future generator) rather than a bespoke store only Readiness Pulse's own pages would know to query.

### Closing screen: a deliberately different beat order

Per the brief's own explicit ordering, `RplCloseScreen.tsx` stages six beats in this order: reinforcement (matched to her pattern and her Q1/Q2 history framing) → the synthesis (three cards: what she's protecting, what's loudest, how ready she is, evidence-first within the readiness card) → the pattern-anchored setup line → "You don't wait for ready. You build it," alone, typed slowly and held → the filling journey progress line (3 of 3, complete) → the membership door. This is deliberately different from Life Signal Check's and Core Values Snapshot's own closing screens, which both open with the progress line — reuses the exact same shared primitives (`components/closing-screen/ClosingScreenPrimitives.tsx`) just staged differently, not a rebuild. The membership door is pattern-framed honest placeholder copy only (no invented pricing/checkout) linking to the real, already-existing `/membership` page; Not Yet gets no primary button at all, only "when you are ready, I will be here" — true, since The Noticing is already running.

### Experiments matched to readiness

Ready Now (real 5-minute daily ritual on Life Signal Check's own loudest signal, or Question 8's pick if nothing was loud, timed to when she said it's hardest) and Ready If It's Small (the identical experiment deliberately shrunk to 2 minutes) both reuse the exact same `cvs_experiment_daily_logs` mechanic and day-3/day-7 follow-up engine Life Signal Check's own experiments use (`CvsDay3FollowUp`/`CvsDay7FollowUp`, extended with a third `'readiness-pulse'` `FollowUpExperience`). Still Deciding gets a real, no-action "Daily Noticing" experiment; Not Yet gets "The Noticing" — both ask the exact same daily yes/no question ("Was there a moment today you wished felt different?"), differing only in framing. The Noticing's own day-7 reflection uses the brief's exact tap-count-tiered copy (0 taps / 1-2 taps / 3+ taps, never fabricated praise, never shame) via a small bespoke component (`RplNotYetDay7.tsx`), since only that one pattern needed count-tiered copy rather than the generic Day7Pattern classification every other pattern shares.

### A real, pre-existing bug found and fixed while verifying this

`app/dashboard/page.tsx` showed a plain empty-state "let's get started" welcome card (`FirstCheckInWelcome`) for any member with zero daily check-ins — regardless of whether they had just completed the entire free arc and started a real Weekly Experiment. A fresh member finishing Readiness Pulse and starting a real experiment could not see it on their own dashboard until they also did an unrelated daily check-in, defeating the entire point of the Active Experiments integration for exactly the audience this build serves. Fixed by fetching `getMyLifestyleExperiments()` in the same existing `Promise.all` batch and gating the welcome card on `!hasCheckins && !hasActiveExperiment` instead of `!hasCheckins` alone — `hasCheckins` itself, and its two other, unrelated usages (the hero's own copy, pop-up-message gating), were left untouched. Pre-existing (affects Core Values Snapshot's and Life Signal Check's own experiments identically, not something Readiness Pulse introduced), but only surfaced by this build's own end-to-end local verification.

Full `npm test` after a fresh `supabase db reset` (migration 141 applied clean) — 305/306 test files, 3434/3435 tests passing; the one failure is the same pre-existing `correlation-engine-integration.test.ts` date-math flake documented throughout this file, reconfirmed in isolation as unrelated. `npm run build` compiled successfully, all routes generated including `/assessments/readiness-pulse`, `/assessments/readiness-pulse/take`, `/assessments/readiness-pulse/results/[sessionId]`, and `/coach/clients/[id]/readiness-pulse/[sessionId]`. New tests: `readiness-pulse-scoring.test.ts` (the full 3x3 derived-pattern table, pick-always-wins precedence, Q8 comparison in all three states, the surprise beat's exact two trigger conditions), `readiness-pulse-copy.test.ts` (divergence framing, membership-door per-pattern shape, the exact Noticing day-7 tap-count copy, zero em dashes), `readiness-pulse-narrative.test.ts` (both drafts genuinely `member_visible: false`), and three new cases in `intelligence-core-coaching-style.test.ts` for the three new tone keywords.

**Verified locally with Playwright** (dev server + local Supabase, fresh throwaway accounts, 390×844 mobile viewport): a real Core Values Snapshot → Life Signal Check (forced loudest signal: Energy, real experiment started for real) → Readiness Pulse run confirmed live: the real enabled "Start the Readiness Pulse" button (no longer disabled "Coming soon") actually navigates and starts the conversation; a never-started Q1/Q2 branch with Q8 matching Life Signal Check's own loudest signal landed Ready Now with a real confirmed-match line and a real Evidence Echo line, zero em dashes; the real 5-minute theory screen; the real six-beat closing screen in the exact specified order with a real enabled membership-door button. A same-account retake with Q3 overdue/Q4 genuinely open/Q7 easily doable (derived: Ready Now) but Q9 Not Yet produced, live: the honest divergence line ("your answers read like ready now, and you said not yet"), the Q3/Q9 surprise beat, an honest Q8 mismatch line (Mind vs. Life Signal Check's own Energy), the real "The Noticing" theory screen, real experiment-cap handling (closed an existing experiment out via the real "Stop early" flow to free a slot), the real Not Yet closing screen (no primary membership button, "I will be here" framing), and confirmed on `/dashboard`: the real Active Experiments section (after the empty-state bug fix above) showing The Noticing's own real daily question. Diagnosis (this session had no production credentials to confirm directly, reasoned from Postgres's own protocol behavior): the SQL Editor sends a pasted multi-statement script as one implicit transaction, and the failure hit on migration 141's very first statement — the only way a hardcoded-UUID insert collides on a fresh attempt is if an earlier attempt had already run the full file to completion and committed it. A guarded, idempotent reconciliation script was provided (preserves the existing catalog row if correct, completes only whatever was actually missing, safe to run regardless of which statements had already succeeded) and **the Osei has run it and confirmed via the verification queries that migration 141 is now fully applied to production**: the catalog row and version row are correct, the unified definition/3 sections/9 questions all exist, and both the `member_coaching_messages_conversation_type_check` and `wellness_coaching_style_profile_tone_preference_check` constraints include Readiness Pulse's additive values. ## Personal Reset Plan — the first monthly-member experience in Rooted Reset (2026-08-02)

The handoff from insight to action: the six-screen creation flow (proposal, why-it-matters, the sized action, the agreement, the closing keepsake), the three-state daily plan card, day-3/day-7 follow-ups through the existing home-card and pop-up surfaces, a coach read-only panel, and an admin test-tools page. Built per a fully locked design brief with the approved action library used verbatim.

### Storage

Three new tables (`supabase/migrations/00000000000142_personal_reset_plan.sql`): `member_reset_plans` (current-state row per member, one partial unique index enforcing "one draft/active plan per member" at the database level), `member_reset_plan_versions` (append-only audit trail, modeled directly on `driver_probe_question_revisions`, migration 110 — full before/after jsonb plus a `decision_evidence` column for Screen 2's focus pick and Screen 4's action-tier shrink), and `member_reset_plan_daily_logs` (the three explicit states — never a boolean — with a real `unique (plan_id, local_date)` constraint and a `day3_response` column carried on the same row, same shape as `cvs_experiment_daily_logs`). `profiles.reset_plan_granted_at` (nullable timestamptz) is the entitlement flag, same shape as migration 85's `welcome_flow_eligible`/`completed_at` pair, enforced server-side in `lib/reset-plan/eligibility.ts` (fail-closed on any error).

Plan content (why-it-matters, the action text, success framing) is stored structurally — `focus_signal` + `action_tier` plus the snapshot columns — and rendered from the approved action library and `lib/reset-plan/copy.ts` at read time, rather than duplicating prose in the database; this keeps one living source of truth for wording, the same discipline the rest of the app already uses.

### Coaching-style guard, and a gap it surfaced

`wellness_coaching_style_profile` gets a `tone_preference_source` column (`'inferred' | 'direct'`) and its `upsert_wellness_coaching_style_profile` RPC is rewritten so a background recompute (`lib/intelligence-core/service.ts`'s `recalculateIntelligenceCore`, which runs on nearly every member action, always calling with the new `source` parameter defaulted to `'inferred'`) can never silently overwrite a row a member has directly stated (`lib/readiness-pulse/coachingStyleWrite.ts`'s `applyRplCoachingStyleStatement`, the one existing direct-write call site, now passes `'direct'`) — even though this experience's own six screens never write a tone preference themselves (Screen 2's focus pick and Screen 4's action-tier shrink are stored as plan decision evidence in `member_reset_plan_versions` instead, exactly per the brief).

Building this exposed a real, pre-existing gap: `wellness_coaching_style_profile` had no member SELECT policy at all (only `coach_read_assigned`/`platform_admin_all`) — confirmed by `tests/intelligence-core-integration.test.ts`'s own existing assertion that this is deliberate (confidence/rationale are coach-internal working data). Rather than loosen that boundary with a blanket grant, migration 142 adds a narrow `get_my_coaching_tone_preference()` security-definer function returning only the one coarse category for the caller's own row; `getMyCoachingTonePreferenceAction` goes through it instead of the table directly.

### Two real, pre-existing bugs found and fixed while verifying this build's own pop-up

Both in the shared Root pop-up priority chain (`app/actions/rootPopupMessages.ts` / `components/dashboard/RootMessagePopupClient.tsx`), neither introduced by this build, both blocking this build's own day-3/day-7 pop-up case from ever being reachable for a realistic member:

1. **Offer starvation**: `findMyPendingRootPopupMessage()` returned the first eligible offer (Core Values Snapshot's own "start it later") with no dismissal check of its own, trusting the single outer `isOfferPopupDue` check on whichever one candidate it returned. Once that one offer had already been shown and dismissed, the whole function returned `null` instead of ever falling through to check Life Signal Check, Readiness Pulse, or the Personal Reset Plan's own pending message — a member who had ever simply declined the Core Values Snapshot Weekly Experiment could never again see **any** later pop-up, of any kind, for the rest of their membership. Fixed by checking each offer's own dismissal inline and continuing to the next experience when it's already resolved.
2. **A real crash**: `RootMessagePopupClient.tsx`'s `isOffer` check was never updated for `'rpl_offer'` when Readiness Pulse (migration 141) introduced it — an `rpl_offer` message fell through into the day3/day7 rendering branch, which unconditionally reads `.logs` (a field only day3/day7 messages carry), throwing `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'filter')` and crashing the entire dashboard. This exact case had been unreachable in practice until bug 1's own fix let the priority chain progress far enough to reach it for the first time.

Both confirmed via a real Playwright run against local Supabase: reproduced live (screenshot of the crash's console error), fixed, reproduced again clean.

## Coach-view hydration fix: shared `formatDisplayDate` helper (2026-08-02)

Fixes the item-13 follow-up above. The root cause was exactly as diagnosed: several coach-view components defined a local `formatTimestamp`/`formatDate`/`formatDateTime` function calling `new Date(iso).toLocaleDateString('en-US', {...})` or `.toLocaleString(...)` with no explicit `timeZone`. Without one, that call resolves against the *host process's own local timezone* — Vercel's server always runs in UTC, a coach's browser runs in whatever zone they are physically in, so the same instant renders as different text server-side vs. client-side and React flags a hydration mismatch. It only surfaced for the history-rich test member because the sparse test accounts have zero rows in the tables these components map over, so the buggy function never actually ran for them.

This codebase had already solved this exact problem once, correctly: `components/case-view/OverlayChart.tsx` and `components/case-view/GoalProgressChart.tsx` each carry their own local `formatDate` with an explicit `timeZone: 'UTC'`, with a comment explaining why. This change generalizes that proven fix into one shared helper and applies it to every other place the same bug existed in the coach view.

### The helper

New file, `lib/time/displayDate.ts`, sibling to the existing `lib/time/localDate.ts` (which solves a different problem: computing which calendar day an instant falls on in a specific member's own timezone for business logic, not display text). `formatDisplayDate(iso: string | null | undefined, options: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions): string` always formats with an explicit `timeZone: 'UTC'`, and returns the honest fallback string `'date not available'` (never `"Invalid Date"`, never throws) for null, undefined, empty string, or an unparseable string.

### Files fixed (33 call sites across 33 files, all in the coach view)

`app/coach/clients/[id]/{RecommendationsPanel,MovementProfilePanel,RootMapPanel,WbsaPanel,AssessmentAssignmentPanel,IntelligencePanel,ReadinessPulsePanel,ConversationPanel,CoachNotesPanel,CoreValuesSnapshotPanel,LongitudinalIntelligencePanel,BodyAssessmentPanel,RootCauseSignalsPanel}.tsx`; `app/coach/clients/[id]/{readiness-pulse,life-signal-check,wbsa,core-values-snapshot}/[sessionId]/page.tsx`; `app/coach/clients/[id]/body-assessments/[assessmentId]/{page,report/page}.tsx` and its `RightPanel/{TimelineSection,PostureFindingsSection,SummarySection,ReviewHistorySection,TrendChart}.tsx`; `app/coach/clients/[id]/prescription/page.tsx`; `app/coach/{review-queue/page,review-queue/[id]/page,corrective-programs/[memberId]/page,protein-review/page}.tsx`; `components/coach-questions/QuestionRow.tsx`; `components/prescription-intelligence/{PrescriptionReviewPanel,PrescriptionIntelligenceCard}.tsx`. Every local `formatTimestamp`/`formatDate`/`formatDateTime` wrapper was deleted once its call sites moved to the shared import; call sites that already null-guarded a nullable timestamp with a ternary (e.g. `session.completedAt ? ... : ''`) kept that exact guard and only had the formatting call inside it swapped.

**Deliberately left untouched**: `app/coach/clients/[id]/PersonalResetPlanPanel.tsx:20` has the identical bug (`new Date(iso).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', day: 'numeric', year: 'numeric' })`, no `timeZone`) but was excluded from this pass per this task's own explicit "do not touch Personal Reset Plan code" instruction. It is a real, live latent bug, left for a separate decision.

**Confirmed out of scope, correctly untouched**: `app/coach/lib.ts`, `app/coach/ClientListPanel.tsx`, `app/coach/clients/[id]/FeedPanel.tsx`, and `app/coach/clients/[id]/page.tsx` all contain look-alike patterns (`new Date(year, month - 1, day).toLocaleDateString(...)`, safe because construction and formatting both use the same runtime's own zone consistently; and the `new Date(new Date().toLocaleString('en-US', { timeZone }))` reparse trick for computing a member's local calendar day, a different, pre-existing business-logic bug already documented by `lib/time/localDate.ts`'s own header comment) — neither is the hydration bug this pass fixes.

### Tests

New file `tests/display-date.test.ts`, 38 tests. Two independent proofs: (1) `formatDisplayDate` produces byte-identical output for the same instant regardless of the test runner's own `process.env.TZ` (asserted with `TZ` set to `America/Los_Angeles`, `Pacific/Kiritimati`, and `UTC` in turn), plus null/undefined/empty-string/malformed-string input all returning the same honest fallback, never `"Invalid Date"`, never throwing; (2) a static source-scan guard (same convention as `tests/assessments-isolation.test.ts`) asserting every one of the 33 fixed files imports `formatDisplayDate` and contains no bare un-timezoned locale call.

**Non-vacuous proof**: `CoachNotesPanel.tsx` was temporarily reverted to its pre-fix body (local `formatTimestamp`, no `timeZone`, no import). Re-running `tests/display-date.test.ts` failed exactly there: `expect(source).toContain('formatDisplayDate')` failed against `CoachNotesPanel.tsx`, 37/38 tests passing, 1 failing for the right reason. The fix was restored (diffed byte-identical against the pre-revert version) and the suite passed 38/38 again.

## Personal Reset Plan Screen 4: shrink control no longer shows tier names (2026-08-02)

## Root Presence System — Prompt 4 (2026-08-03)

Makes Root feel present rather than printed: first-person voice fixed everywhere it was previously third-person/plural, brief "thinking" beats before Moment-screen reveals, Root-voiced loading text on Moment skeletons, four real memory-callback types, a one-time no-guilt return greeting, and honest discovery presentation for genuinely new correlation findings. Full detail (data sources, mechanics, and the reasoning behind each design choice) is now documented in `docs/motion-experience-bible.md` §15 — this entry summarizes what shipped.

### Voice audit

First-person "I" replaced first-person-plural "we" or third-person "Root" self-reference in every surface this prompt named: the dashboard's "From Root" card (`lib/root-coaching-engine/templates.ts`, ~14 strings), Reset Plan's own copy (`lib/reset-plan/copy.ts`, entry card/proposal/agreement/miss-handling), "What We're Noticing" and the Insights hub's shell copy, Case View's header/investigation/empty-state copy (`components/case-view/CaseHeader.tsx`, `InvestigationPanel.tsx`, `lib/case-view/emptyState.ts`), and the Daily Brief's sleep/stress summary lines (`lib/coaching-engine/morningBrief.ts`). Factual content (counts, dates, section meaning) was never changed, only how Root says it. Deliberately left untouched: `lib/feed/encouragement.ts`'s generic aphorism pool (its own header comment documents this as intentionally non-personalized) and the many scattered third-person "Root will/can" captions across food-lens/wearables/movement/restaurant UI — genuinely instructional feature copy outside this prompt's named surfaces (Daily Brief, Noticing, Case View, Insights, day-3/day-7, assessment results, coaching copy), flagged for whichever future prompt does the full-app audit (Prompt 7).

### Thinking moments

`components/closing-screen/KeyFindingReveal.tsx` gained an optional `thinkingText` prop (first view only, tap-anywhere-skippable, still under a second) — wired into the 3 generic-engine results pages (WBSA, the points-scored engine, Primal Pattern Diet Type). CVS/LSC/RPL's own closing screens needed no new component: a thinking line is simply prepended to `ConversationFlow`'s existing message array, conditioned on the screen's own first-view flag.

### Loading with purpose

`components/PageSkeleton.tsx` gained an optional `message` prop, wired into the 5 Moment-classified `loading.tsx` skeletons and the 3 take-flow skeletons that previously shipped with zero text, plus `AssessmentWizard`'s bare `checkingResume` spinner. The 17 Tool-classified skeletons were deliberately left untouched (already the correct Tool pattern). The three takers' duplicated "One moment, Root is putting this together" line is now one shared, first-person constant, `ROOT_FINISHING_LABEL` (`lib/reveal/copy.ts`).

### Memory callbacks

New `lib/memory-callback/` (`types.ts`, `data.ts`, `copy.ts`) — four pure builders (`buildGoalCallback`, `buildTenureCallback`, `buildDay3ContrastCallback`, `buildFindingCallback`), each returning `null` whenever the backing data doesn't exist, 100% built on existing reusable queries except one genuinely new one (`fetchTenureCallbackContext`'s unbounded first-check-in date — the existing `firstEverCheckinDate` is bounded to a 90-day scoring lookback, the wrong shape for "how long have you been here"). Wired into: the Daily Brief's `encouragingMessage` slot (tenure, lowest priority in a new chain — see below), Case View's header (tenure only, never the goal callback there since the goal is already the header's own title), and the CVS/LSC/RPL day-7 Root pop-up messages (goal callback, via a new shared `appendCallback` helper and a `goalCallback` field threaded through `app/actions/rootPopupMessages.ts`'s discriminated union). `buildDay3ContrastCallback`/`buildFindingCallback` are built and tested but not yet wired into a speaking spot beyond the module itself.

### No-guilt return greeting

New `member_return_greetings(member_id, gap_start_local_date, shown_at)` (migration 143), keyed on the member's last real check-in date before the gap so the same gap episode can never earn the greeting twice. Threshold: `daysSinceLastCheckin >= 3` (`RETURN_GREETING_MIN_GAP_DAYS`, `lib/return-greeting/copy.ts`). `lib/return-greeting/data.ts`'s `tryMarkReturnGreetingShown` is an atomic `insert ... on conflict do nothing` (race-safe under concurrent requests). Wins the Daily Brief's `encouragingMessage` slot outright, ahead of a streak or a memory callback: "I'm glad you're back." — zero mention of the gap length or a missed-day count. A companion data-only `update` in migration 143 fixed two dormant, never-actually-rendered guilt-adjacent `ai_rules` seed rows (migration 053: "It has been a couple of days... keeps things on track" and "We have missed you") to the same first-person, no-guilt standard, so a future surface reading that table inherits correct copy. No other guilt/streak/"missed" language was found anywhere actually rendered to a member (`lib/feed/streakIntelligence.ts`'s `buildStreakMessage` already correctly says "No worries...").

### Discovery moments

New `member_discovery_moments(member_id, signal_key, surfaced_at)` (migration 143) marks a correlation finding as already presented once. `lib/discovery-moments/select.ts` (pure) and `service.ts` (I/O) reuse Case View's own `buildFindings` read path verbatim, filtered to `tier >= 2` and to signal keys not yet in the new table — zero new correlation/trend logic, the engines are untouched. Deliberately **not** wired into the Root pop-up chain (`app/actions/rootPopupMessages.ts`) — that system is scoped to messages expecting an answer/acknowledge/act, and a 5th message kind there would be starved behind day-3/day-7/offer messages for any member mid-experiment. Instead, new `RootDiscoveryCard` (`components/dashboard/RootDiscoveryCard.tsx`) takes its own slot in the dashboard's "What Root Is Noticing" carousel, reusing the existing `NoticingTile`/`NoticingSheet` tap-to-reveal shell "From Root" already established: "Root noticed something" / "Want to see?" on the tile, a thinking beat then the real finding sentence (`ConversationFlow`) in the sheet. Marked surfaced server-side the instant it's decided to show (same precedent as the Root pop-up offer's own "write on mount" fix); after that the same finding just appears, unflagged, in Case View's own findings list.

### Bible update

`docs/motion-experience-bible.md` gained §15 documenting all of the above (memory callback types + data sources, discovery/thinking/return-greeting mechanics, the loading-purpose convention), and §14's Implementation Map now marks Prompt 4 `(Complete.)`.

## Dashboard Evolution — Prompt 5 (2026-08-03)

Makes the Home dashboard (`app/dashboard/page.tsx`) a living screen — same data, same engines, same navigation, no reveal pacing, no new waits — per `docs/motion-experience-bible.md`'s new §11a-§11e (§11's old speculative bullets superseded; §14 now marks Prompt 5 complete). No engine, no calculation, no threshold, and no navigation/bottom-nav/Quick-Actions ordering changed anywhere in this task.

**New, pure logic modules** (`apps/consumer-web-app/lib/dashboard/`), no I/O, fully unit-tested:
- `greeting.ts` — `buildGreetingLine`: a short, Root-voiced second line under the existing hero greeting, varying by real time band and whether today's check-in exists (`hasCheckinToday`, already-fetched data, no new query), rotating deterministically by the member's own local date (not randomness, not request time) so the same day never flickers between lines but the line still changes day to day.
- `prioritization.ts` — `orderTodayCards(hasCheckinToday)`: promotes the check-in prompt to the lead of the Today zone when not done yet, or today's real progress/reflection content once it is; `NOTICING_CARD_ORDER`: the Root Discovery card always leads the "What Root Is Noticing" carousel ahead of routine cards. Both are within-zone reorderings only (no zone swaps, no navigation changes) so every card stays exactly as reachable as before.
- `timeOfDayPalette.ts` — `heroOverlayForGreeting`/`pageBackgroundForGreeting`: a few-percentage-point tint shift (forest green undertone in the morning, gold/amber in the evening) on the hero's existing legibility overlay and the page background wash, keyed off the same `greetingWord` the hero photo already switches on so the two can never disagree. Still entirely within the locked forest green/gold/cream palette.

**Wired into `app/dashboard/page.tsx`**: `heroGreetingLine`/`todayCardOrder` computed from data the page already fetches (zero new queries on the per-request render path); the Today zone's four blocks (Daily Brief, assigned programs, DailyWellnessSection, the numbers/check-in-prompt block) now render via a small ordered map instead of a fixed sequence; `RootDiscoveryCard` moved to the front of the Noticing carousel's JSX (it already self-gates to nothing when there's no genuinely new finding, so this costs nothing on any other day and needed no new fetch to decide).

**Ambient motion** (Bible §10/§11d), both gated behind Prompt 1's `useLowPowerMode` (reduced motion, low battery, or a low-end device signal all disable them), and deliberately the only two ambient/idle elements live on this page at once:

Same conservative gating as every other callback: each builder still independently returns `null` when its own real data doesn't exist.

## Face ID login (passkeys) + logo intro stall fix (2026-08-04)

Two independent tasks, run together. Neither blocked the other.

### Part A — Face ID login (Supabase passkeys)

Native Supabase Auth passkey support (beta, confirmed against current Supabase docs via live fetch, not assumed): `@supabase/supabase-js` upgraded `2.44.4` → `2.112.0`, `@supabase/ssr` `0.4.0` → `0.12.4` (its own peer requirement is `^2.111.0`). No custom WebAuthn layer, no third-party auth provider — only `supabase.auth.registerPasskey()` / `supabase.auth.signInWithPasskey()` / `supabase.auth.passkey.{list,delete}()`, gated behind the required `auth: { experimental: { passkey: true } }` opt-in flag now set on `lib/supabase/client.ts`'s browser client (the only client that needs it — WebAuthn ceremonies only ever run in the browser).

**Enrollment** — new `app/profile/PasskeyEnrollment.tsx`, wired into Profile's existing "Account" card (`app/profile/page.tsx`). Checks `lib/passkey/support.ts`'s `isPasskeySupported()` (the actual platform-authenticator check, `PublicKeyCredential.isUserVerifyingPlatformAuthenticatorAvailable()`, not just "does WebAuthn exist") on mount; an unsupported browser gets a short, plain, disabled explanation instead of a dead button. A supported browser can enable Face ID, sees each enrolled device listed by its own `friendly_name`, and can remove any of them.

**Login** — new `components/auth/PasskeyLoginButton.tsx`, sitting alongside (never replacing) password login on `app/(auth)/login/page.tsx`. Hidden outright (not disabled) when unsupported, since there's nothing useful to explain to a signed-out member on this specific screen. A cancelled or failed ceremony (`lib/passkey/errors.ts`'s `isPasskeyCancelled`, matching the documented `ERROR_CEREMONY_ABORTED` code and the raw `NotAllowedError`/`AbortError` DOMException names) lands back on the normal form with no error shown at all — "no error drama," per this task's own requirement. A genuine failure (e.g. the project hasn't enabled passkeys yet) shows a specific, friendly message via `getFriendlyPasskeyError`, mirroring `lib/auth/errors.ts`'s existing message-matching convention (supabase-js does not re-export `WebAuthnError`/`isWebAuthnError` at the top level this app imports from, so errors are matched by `.code`/`.name` shape instead of the class).

Since `signInWithPasskey()` only runs in the browser (WebAuthn has no server-side equivalent) but the post-login role/onboarding routing and the branded entry-animation cookie are server-side concerns, `app/actions/auth.ts` gained `completePasskeyLogin()` — the same tail `signIn()` already ran (`resolvePostLoginPath` + the one-shot `mef_entry_login` cookie + `redirect()`), extracted into a shared `redirectWithEntryAnimation()` helper so a Face ID login and a password login always hand off to the app identically. Confirmed no session-cookie race: `@supabase/ssr`'s browser client persists a new session via a synchronous `document.cookie` write inside its own storage adapter (read from its own source, not assumed), so the session is already visible to the very next Server Action call.

**Enabling the feature itself**: this session has no Supabase personal access token available to call the Management API (the CLI installed locally is authenticated for read-only project listing, but is a full API-version behind and has no passkey-config command; extracting its stored token to hand-roll API calls against the live production project was correctly blocked as a sensitive action this session shouldn't take unilaterally). **This needs one manual dashboard step before it will do anything** — see the report given to the user for the exact clicks. Until then, `registerPasskey()`/`signInWithPasskey()` fail with Supabase's own `passkey_disabled` code, which this build already renders as a calm, specific message ("Face ID Login isn't turned on for this account yet...") rather than a broken/dead button — confirmed for real against local Supabase, which is in the same "not enabled" state a not-yet-toggled production project would be (see Verified, below).

### Part B — logo intro stall fix

**Real cause, found by reproducing it first** (not guessed): the branded "Rooted Reset" entry-animation overlay (`components/entry/RootResetEntryAnimation.tsx`) was already a genuine fixed-clock animation with no data dependency beyond an already-capped 300ms name-fetch wait — that part of the original bug report's hypothesis was wrong. Reproduced with Playwright + Chrome DevTools Protocol network throttling and artificial route delays against the local dev server (`member.one@example.test`, real local Supabase): the *real* cause is that the overlay is mounted in the root layout on top of `{children}`, and a fresh login's redirect is a client-side navigation that can still be in flight when the overlay's own fixed timer ends. Under a slow connection, the overlay would finish and unmount on schedule while the *previous* page (the plain `/login` form) was still what was actually mounted underneath — confirmed on video/screenshot: the login form visibly reappeared for several seconds before the browser finally jumped to `/dashboard`. Separately, `app/layout.tsx` was also doing a second, non-deduped Supabase profile lookup inside an unSuspended `await` that blocked the entire app shell (every route's own `loading.tsx` included) behind a database round trip on every fresh login or reopen — a real, if smaller, contributor.

**Fix, timing behavior only, no animation/artwork/choreography changes**: `app/layout.tsx` no longer looks up the member's first name server-side at all (`RootResetEntryGate`'s own existing client-side `getEntryAnimationGreeting()` fetch, already capped at 300ms with a graceful fallback, now always does that instead) — one blocking Supabase call removed from the critical path of every fresh login/reopen. `components/entry/RootResetEntryGate.tsx` now tracks whether the token driving an activation was already known at this component's own SSR render (`initialEntryToken`) or was discovered later via a live `document.cookie` read — the latter means a client-side navigation to a not-yet-rendered page is still in flight underneath the overlay. When the branded animation's own fixed duration ends and that's still true, the gate no longer unmounts and reveals whatever's behind it; it bridges with the app's existing design-system loading skeleton (`components/PageSkeleton.tsx`, the same "calm shimmer + bottom nav" treatment every other route's `loading.tsx` already uses) until the real navigation lands (`usePathname()` changing is the exact, earliest-possible signal), capped by a new `RESET_ENTRY_BRIDGE_MAX_MS` (8000ms) safety timeout so a navigation that never completes can't trap the member behind the skeleton either. The reopen-after-gap case (Page Visibility, no navigation ever pending) and a token already known at first paint (a fresh full-page load) both correctly skip the bridge entirely — there is nothing to wait for in either case.

### Verified

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Repo-root `npm run lint` — 0 errors, same 90 pre-existing warnings, none in touched/new files. `npm run build` compiled successfully, all routes generated including `/login` and `/profile`. Full `npx vitest run` after a fresh `supabase db reset` — 323/324 test files, 3689/3690 tests passing; the one failure is the same pre-existing `correlation-engine-integration.test.ts` Spearman date-math flake documented throughout this file's history, unrelated to this change. Two new test files: `tests/passkey-errors.test.ts` (14 tests, pure — cancel-detection and every documented error code's copy, pinned) and 2 new cases appended to `tests/entry-animation-rule.test.ts` (bridge-cap constant, bounded and positive).

**Local Playwright verification** (dev server + local Supabase, real seeded `member.one@example.test`, 390×844 mobile viewport): a Chrome DevTools Protocol virtual platform authenticator (`WebAuthn.addVirtualAuthenticator`, simulating a phone's Face ID) made both "Sign in with Face ID" (login) and "Enable Face ID Login" (profile) render correctly; without one, both correctly stay hidden/absent (`isPasskeySupported()` returns false) and password login is completely unaffected. Local Supabase's GoTrue predates passkey support entirely, so a real enrollment attempt against it returned Supabase's own `passkey_disabled` code end-to-end — rendered as this build's calm, specific copy ("Face ID Login isn't turned on for this account yet. Please check back soon."), not a crash or a raw error, which is exactly the "works the moment the dashboard toggle is flipped" state this task asked for. The genuine cancel/success WebAuthn ceremony itself can only be driven against a project with passkeys actually enabled (production only, and this session was told not to log into or test the live site), so `isPasskeyCancelled`/`getFriendlyPasskeyError` were instead proven directly against every documented Supabase error shape via the new unit tests.

For the intro fix: reproduced the stall first (throttled network, `~6.4s` gap between the branded animation ending and the dashboard actually appearing, with the stale `/login` form visibly reappearing in between — screenshotted), then reproduced again post-fix under the same conditions and confirmed the gap now shows the app's own loading skeleton ("Just a moment.") the entire time instead, with zero stale-content reveal, screenshotted. A separate run with an artificially delayed dashboard response (6000ms, network otherwise fast) isolated and confirmed the exact hand-off moment: the branded animation's own overlay div (`aria-hidden="true"`) is replaced by the skeleton bridge div at the animation's natural ~3.6-4s finish, and the skeleton itself is replaced by real dashboard content the instant `pathname` actually changes to `/dashboard`. Local Supabase was reset (`supabase db reset`) after driving the app manually, before the final test run, per this repo's own established convention for real-database integration tests.

**Not done this task**: the Supabase dashboard toggle itself (needs the user's own login — see the report for exact clicks), and live-site verification of either part (explicitly out of scope this task — "Local testing only... I will verify the live site myself").

**Deployed**: pushed to `origin/main`. Vercel auto-deploys `main` to production per this repo's established pattern (confirmed in every prior entry above) — this session did not run `vercel inspect`/`curl` against the live site to confirm the deployment landed, per this task's own explicit instruction not to test or verify the live site.


## Root Movement, Level 1 — six ready-made sessions (2026-08-13)

Six fixed movement sessions, global, available to every member with no assessment behind them and no coach approval in front of them. Assembled entirely from the exercise catalog and corrective tagging that already existed (migrations 119/120/127/128). This is the member-facing exercise experience; it adds no intelligence.

**Audit first, two premise mismatches found and reported before building.** (1) The Your Move video player is NOT in My Programs. `/programs` is coach-assigned workouts (migration 82) and renders no video at all; the real tap-to-play player lived inside `components/exercise-library/ExerciseDetailView.tsx` as a private `TapToPlayVideo` function, used by the Exercise Library detail screen. (2) Corrective programs have no member-facing surface at all — `app/coach/corrective-programs/*` is coach-only, so "video playback used by corrective programs in My Programs" describes nothing that exists. Also noted: the Your Move catalog contains no breathing exercises, so no session can open with breathwork.

**Sessions are data, not code.** Migration 153 adds `movement_session_templates` (session_key, name, one-sentence description, target duration range, sort_order, is_active) and `movement_session_template_slots` (ordered slots keyed on the same `(provider, external_id)` natural key every other exercise-referencing table uses, with a time-OR-reps prescription and a rest interval, enforced by check constraint). Swapping an exercise or a prescription is an UPDATE, never a deploy. The migration asserts its own seed integrity in a `do $$` block: every slot must resolve to a catalog exercise with `has_video`, none may be spinal-flexion / release-tier / power-tier / high-strain, and the distinct-exercise count must stay under 40. A bad edit fails the migration rather than reaching a member.

**The six, all landing inside their own stated target ranges** (computed from the real slots, 4s per rep): morning_mobility 11.3 min (11 slots), desk_reset 10.4 (10), hip_back_reset 14.1 (14), shoulder_neck_reset 10.6 (11), core_foundation 12.1 (12), recovery_day 17.9 (16). **39 distinct exercises across all six**, so the video quota stays comfortable and a member meets the same movements again instead of a new one every screen. Assembly rules enforced by test, not by intention: mobility before stability, stability before strength, core work last where a session has any, no crunches or loaded spinal flexion anywhere, nothing above moderate strain, no release/SMR tier, no external load, bodyweight/chair/wall only.

**One table for completion records**, per the build: `member_movement_session_runs` (member, session_key, started_at, completed_at, `skipped_exercise_ids text[]`). A run with `completed_at` null is a mid-session exit, which is an ordinary state — there is no abandonment flag, no reason column and no note column, which is what makes "keys, ids, timestamps and counts only" a property of the schema rather than a promise. Every start is its own row, so a member repeats any session any day as often as she likes.

**The player reuses the existing one.** `TapToPlayVideo` was EXTRACTED out of `ExerciseDetailView.tsx` into `components/exercise-library/TapToPlayVideo.tsx` and imported by both call sites, rather than reimplemented — so tap-to-play, the ~10min `exercise_catalog.video_url` cache, and the poster/cues fallbacks behave identically in both places, and there is still exactly one component in the product that can spend Your Move quota. It gained two props: `heightClassName` (the two screens want different media heights) and `autoPlayKey` (advancing to the next exercise resets it to idle, so quota is spent by taps and never by advancing). Session cues are carried even for has-video exercises, unlike the library's normalizer, because a mid-session video failure is exactly when a member most needs to be told what to do.

**Entry point**: a nav-link card at the top of `/movement`'s existing `CardStack`, alongside Exercise Library and Movement Profile — the audit's answer for where this naturally belongs. It renders regardless of whether the member has ever checked in, unlike the generated session below it, and it is gated on `listActiveSessionTemplates` returning rows so it does not appear at all before the migration lands. New routes: `/movement/sessions` (the six) and `/movement/sessions/[sessionKey]` (lineup, player, completion). No streaks, no badges, no timer, no score, no celebration; nothing notices or mentions leaving part way through.

**Analytics on the existing pipeline.** Four additive event types widening the `member_wellness_events` constraint and `is_product_analytics_event_type` (same rule migrations 146/147/150/151/152 followed): `movement_session_viewed` (sessionKey, exerciseCount), `movement_session_started` (sessionKey), `movement_exercise_skipped` (sessionKey, exerciseId), `movement_session_completed` (sessionKey, skipCount). Four new payload keys on the existing allowlist. Every value is validated server-side against the templates table and that session's own slots before it can reach a payload.

**Explicitly not done, as instructed**: the engine's `movement` action type stays BLOCKED (`lib/coaching-direction/types.ts` untouched); nothing was added to the Priority Card, the Weekly Root Review or the pop-up chain; no gamification; no coach approval; the corrective program system was not touched.

**Tests added**: `tests/movement-session-templates.test.ts` (14, real seeded rows — the six exist, every slot resolves to a real videoed exercise, no crunch/release/power/high-strain, ordering rule, durations in range, vocabulary under 40), `tests/movement-session-runs.test.ts` (17, real RLS — global templates, lineup resolution, start/skip/complete, idempotent skip, complete-once, mid-session exit, same-day repeats, cross-member isolation, all four events and the analytics view), `tests/movement-session-privacy.test.ts` (12, four layers — schema columns, sanitizer, call-site source scan, real end-to-end output scanned for health content by value — plus a re-assertion from this feature's own side that the movement action type is still blocked and that nothing was wired into the ladder or the Weekly Review), `tests/movement-session-fails-closed.test.ts` (5, a stub client that errors on every query, proving every read and write path returns empty/null and never throws where the migration has not been applied).

**Two guard tests proven by deliberately breaking them and restoring.** (1) Repointed a `core_foundation` slot at the catalog's "Lying oblique crunch" (`spinal_flexion_core = true`): "contains no crunch or loaded spinal flexion anywhere" failed by name; restored, 14/14 pass. (2) Emptied `BLOCKED_ACTION_TYPES` in `lib/coaching-direction/types.ts`: four tests failed — Part 1's own three (`tests/coaching-direction-hierarchy.test.ts`) plus this build's re-assertion; restored, 59/59 pass.

**The ordering rule caught a real defect during the build**: `desk_reset` originally had "Psoas stretch" (a pure stretch) after "Sitting Pelvic tilts" (tagged mobility+strength), running the tiers backwards. The test failed by name, the two slots were swapped in the migration, and the lineup is correct as seeded.

**Three pre-existing guard tests updated, not weakened**, because `TapToPlayVideo` moved file: `tests/exercise-video-fallback-graceful.test.ts` and `tests/exercise-video-poster-placeholder-wiring.test.ts` now read the extracted file (the fallback test now guards both call sites at once rather than only the detail screen), and `tests/subhead-contrast-ratio.test.ts` caught the new player using the superseded `#6B7A72` subhead color, now `#4F645A`.

**Verified**: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Repo-root `npm run lint` — 0 errors, same 90 pre-existing warnings, none in touched or new files. Full `npx vitest run` — 355 test files, 4625 tests, 4624 passing; the one failure is the same pre-existing `correlation-engine-integration.test.ts` Spearman date-math flake documented throughout this file's history, unrelated to this change. `npm run build` compiled successfully with both new routes generated (`/movement/sessions` 143 B, `/movement/sessions/[sessionKey]` 5.29 kB).

**Local end-to-end verification with Playwright** (new committed script `scripts/screenshots/verify-root-movement.mjs`, dev server + local Supabase, real seeded `member.one`, 390×844): 12/12 checks passed — entry card present on `/movement`, all six sessions listed with six duration labels, `desk_reset` showing its full 10-exercise lineup, Begin starting the session, the first three exercises each rendering a real video surface (`Play exercise video` button), one exercise skipped, session walked to completion with the calm acknowledgment ("That is the session."), no hype and no em dash in the completion copy, leaving mid-session showing no warning or lost-progress message, and no movement recommendation anywhere on Home. ## Root Movement, Level 1 — the six lineups refined and applied (2026-08-13)

The follow-up the previous entry said was coming: the owner reviewed the six lineups and they were rebuilt so each session is a clearly different solution rather than the same library rearranged six ways. **Nothing structural changed.** No new table, column, event type or session; no rename; no touch to recommendation logic; the engine's `movement` action type stays BLOCKED. Migration 154 rewrites the ordered slots of the six templates seeded by 153, plus two member-facing description sentences a lineup change made untrue. That is exactly the shape migration 153 promised: swapping an exercise or a prescription is an UPDATE, never a deploy. **No app code changed at all in this build.**

**What each session now is, and what moved.**

- **Morning Mobility, 11 slots to 9, 11.3 to 11.4 min.** It read as "Morning Stretch": nine of eleven slots were static holds. Removed Child's pose, Sphinx pose, Knee to Chest left and right, Standing Hamstring left and right. Added Reclined windshield wipers (the spinal rotation it had none of), **Bridge pose** (hip and spine extension after a night curled up) and **Lateral leg swing** (standing hip movement, chair for balance), plus Bird Dog before the closing Dead Bug. Cat cow lengthened 75s to 90s.
- **Desk Reset, 10 slots, 10.4 to 10.7 min. The Wall Sit is gone.** A one-minute wall sit is a held ninety degrees of hip and knee flexion, the exact shape she has been in all day. The session now ends in extension and on the posterior chain: Goal Post Squeeze then **Hip hinge**, standing, glute and hamstring driven. Added `chair Twists` for thoracic rotation, since a chair takes rotation away before it takes anything else. Neck, chest, thoracic, hip-flexor and pelvic work all kept. Still nothing on the floor.
- **Hip and Back Reset, 14 slots, 14.1 min, unchanged.** Same fourteen exercises, same prescriptions. **Ordering only**: the two standing hamstring stretches moved from slots 9 and 10 to slots 1 and 2, so a fourteen-minute session no longer sends her off the floor and back down again in the middle of it.
- **Shoulder and Neck Reset, 11 slots to 12, 10.6 to 11.6 min.** Thoracic mobility was NOT sufficient: the session had thoracic extension (Puppy pose) and nothing for thoracic rotation, the range a desk-bound upper back loses first. `chair Twists` added. Arm swings moved from slot 4 to slot 9 so the seated stretch block runs uninterrupted and the dynamic arm work sits next to the work it prepares. **The finish was reviewed and deliberately left alone**: Goal Post Squeeze is cued "down and together, without shrugging", and Wall Push Ups after it protract the scapula rather than piling more retraction on. Neck work is still only the three slots it was; nothing was added there.
- **Core Foundation, 12 slots to 10, 12.1 to 12.2 min.** Slots 4 to 7 were a balance walk, a squat and a wall sit before any trunk work at all. **Heel to toe walk removed** (a balance drill is not trunk control, and it was the only 'intermediate' item in any of the six). **Bodyweight Squat removed** (it was asked to justify itself and could not; nothing in a squat teaches a beginner where her ribs and pelvis are). **Wall Sit removed** (an isometric quad hold, same reasoning). The time went to pelvic control, dead bug, bird dog, anti-extension and lateral stability. **Dead Bug goes 60s to 110s**, because that is where the learning is. The bridge sits before the dead bug rather than after, which is the one place this session departs from the order a coach would say out loud: the assembly rule is strength before core work and core last, and Glute Bridge is tagged strength.
- **Recovery Day, 16 slots to 9, 17.9 to 15.8 min.** It was the other sessions done slowly. Removed the knee to chest, figure four, standing hamstring and lateral neck pairs it borrowed from Hip and Back Reset, Morning Mobility and Desk Reset. It now opens supported and supine on **Reclined butterfly**, holds run 60 to 180 seconds instead of 40 to 75, nothing is standing, nothing is bilateral to count through, and it still ends on three minutes of Corpse pose. Happy baby was dropped as redundant with the new opener, which also kept the vocabulary inside its ceiling.

**Four exercises are new to Root Movement**, all already in the production catalog with `has_video = true`, all beginner, all bodyweight or chair, none release/power tier, none high strain, none spinal flexion: Bridge pose, Lateral leg swing, Hip hinge, Reclined butterfly. **Three leave the vocabulary**: Wall Sit, Bodyweight Squat, Heel to toe walk. Distinct vocabulary 39 to 39, total slots 74 to 64.

**A real gap, recorded rather than filled. VIDEO GAP: breathing / bracing.** Core Foundation should open on a breathing or bracing drill and Recovery Day on a breathing downshift. The production library does contain two suitable exercises, `mef_custom` "Supine TVA Draw-In Breathing" and "4-Point TVA Vacuum", and **both have `has_video = false`**; no catalog row anywhere is tagged `program_section = 'breathing'` (confirmed by querying production, not assumed). Nothing was created, faked, placeholdered or silently substituted. Core Foundation opens on Cat cow (find a neutral spine before loading one) and Recovery Day on Reclined butterfly, whose own instructions are "rest your arms at your sides with palms up, close your eyes and relax" — the best programming-appropriate options that have verified video today.

**The migration asserts more than 153 did.** Same checks (every slot resolves to a videoed catalog exercise, nothing spinal-flexion / release / power / high-strain, vocabulary under 40) plus two this refinement made worth having: that no template ended up with zero slots after the delete-and-reinsert, and that **each session's computed length still lands inside its own stated target range**, using the same arithmetic `lib/movement-sessions/duration.ts` uses.

**A guard caught a real error during this build, before any test ran.** The first `supabase db reset` failed with "Root Movement lineups: 40 distinct exercises, the vocabulary is meant to stay under 40". The lineup was wrong, not the guard: Recovery Day was carrying both Reclined butterfly and Happy baby, two supine passive hip openers doing the same job. The redundant one was dropped. **The threshold was not raised to accommodate the design.**

**A second guard proven by deliberately breaking it and restoring.** Repointed `desk_reset` slot 1 at "Hip hinge" (tagged mobility+strength) in the local database: the ordering test failed by name, "desk_reset: slot 2 (Lateral neck stretch (left)) comes after a higher tier", 1 failed / 13 passed. Restored, 14/14 pass.

## Daily Reset "Your body" screen: the meals-skipped follow-up, and a Continue that never explains itself (2026-08-14)

**The report, confirmed in the data before anything was changed.** "How many meals did you skip today?" (`checkin_probe.meals_skipped_today`, a `count` question offering 0/1/2/3) had a follow-up, "Which meal(s) did you skip?" (`checkin_probe.skipped_meal_which`), that was stored as `single_select` over Breakfast / Lunch / Dinner / **"More than one"**. Answer 2 and there was no way to say which two: tapping a second meal deselected the first, and the one option that acknowledged the situation recorded nothing about which meals they were. The prompt itself says "meal(s)". The question was authored as a multi-select and stored as a single-select. Read directly off the production bank, not inferred from the migration file.

**One correction to the report, stated because it changes what actually had to be fixed.** The dead Continue was NOT caused by the meals question. Rotating probes are optional units and have never gated Continue. On the "Your body" screen the blocking units are the "Any discomfort today?" gate and, if she says yes, the body-outline location plus severity. A member working on the meals question with the discomfort gate still unanswered somewhere else on the same screen got a disabled Continue **with nothing on screen saying why** — which from her side is exactly "tapping Continue does nothing at all with no feedback." Both faults are real, both are fixed, and the second one is the one that made the first feel unrecoverable.

**A silent block is now structurally unwritable.** `CheckinUnit.required: boolean` is gone. In its place is `blockedReason: string | null` — null means optional, a string means it blocks Continue AND is the line the member reads. There is no longer any way to mark a unit blocking without supplying the sentence, so this fails at compile time rather than at review time. `screenBlockedReason()` returns the first blocking-and-unanswered unit's reason; `CheckinWizard` renders it inside the sticky footer directly above the button (so it is on screen at the moment a dead Continue is tapped, not scrolled away with the question), with `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-describedby` on the button. `continueHelperText()` is the whole rule as one pure, testable decision: disabled and not saving always yields a non-empty line, falling back to "Answer the questions above to continue." if a screen ever forgets one. Both flows also stopped exempting their final screen from the completeness check (`isLastScreen ? saving : !screenComplete` became `saving || !screenComplete`).

**The count-matching rule is data-driven, not keyed to the meals question.** New `lib/daily-checkin-adaptive/followUpValidation.ts`: any `multi_select` follow-up whose parent is a `count` question must have exactly as many options selected as the parent's number. A coach pairing another count parent with a multi-select follow-up in /coach/questions gets the same validation with no deploy. It fails OPEN on every shape it does not understand (parent absent from today's plan, parent unanswered, parent not a count, follow-up not multi-select, non-integer or negative answer), and clamps to the number of options offered, because a validation nobody can satisfy is the bug being fixed. Copy: "Select 2 meals." when short, "Select only 2 meals, or change the number above." when over, singular at 1, no em dashes.

**A second contradiction of the same family, fixed while in there.** Answer 2 meals, pick two, then set the count back to 0: the follow-up correctly disappeared, but its two selections were still submitted, so the database said both that no meals were skipped and that the ones skipped were breakfast and lunch. Any follow-up that is no longer eligible but has an answer on file (in state or from an earlier save today) now has its stored row overwritten with an empty answer, generically, for every follow-up rather than for this one.

**THE FULL BUG-CLASS SWEEP.** All 88 rows of the live production bank were read and every one of the 9 rows carrying a `requires`/`excludes` rule was classified.

| Follow-up | Parent (type) | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `skipped_meal_which` (single_select) | `meals_skipped_today` (**count**) | **THE BUG. Fixed**: multi_select, "More than one" deleted, count-matched. |
| `digestive_symptom_type` (single_select) | `digestion_rating` (**scale**, a number type) | **Same class. Fixed**: multi_select, "More than one" deleted. Bloating and gas on one morning was not recordable. No count-matching applies, since a rating of 2 does not imply two symptoms. |
| `crash_timing` (single_select, has "More than once") | `energy_crash_today` (boolean) | **Reported, deliberately NOT changed.** Its parent is a plain yes/no, so no validation can conflict and nothing can get stuck. "More than once" is a genuine answer about WHEN, not a stand-in for a list. Converting it is a product decision, not a bug fix. Say the word and it takes one migration. |
| `alcohol_drinks_count` (count) | `alcohol_present` (boolean) | Clean. Nothing to contradict. |
| `emotional_load_source` | `emotional_load_today` (single_select) | Clean. |
| `got_up_hourly` (boolean) | `desk_hours_today` (single_select) | Clean. |
| `late_eating_reason` | `last_meal_timing` (single_select) | Clean. |
| `what_changed` | `medication_or_supplement_change` (boolean) | Clean. |
| `what_kept_you_up` | `bedtime_later_than_wanted` (boolean) | Clean. |

Also checked and cleared: the other four `count` questions (`caffeine_servings`, `night_waking_count`, `bowel_movement_frequency_today`, `alcohol_drinks_count`) have no follow-ups at all; `meals_with_protein`'s "All of them" and `movement_type_today`'s "A mix of both" are genuine aggregate answers to how-many/what-kind questions, not workarounds, and were left alone.

**Migration 157** converts both questions in place (not retire-and-replace — answers live in the generic jsonb `daily_checkin_probe_answers.value`, exactly the reasoning migration 115 used for the craving question), migrates every recorded answer (a bare string becomes a one-element array; `"more_than_one"` becomes an empty array, i.e. "which ones was not recorded", which for the meals question loses nothing at all since the number is stored on the parent's own answer row), and RAISEs NOTICE with the exact row counts it touched rather than rewriting silently. It then adds three assertions that fail the migration rather than let the class back in through a plain coach data edit: no active single_select still leans on a "more than one" stand-in (crash_timing excepted, by name, with its reasoning in the file); no active `count` parent has an active `single_select` follow-up; and every multi_select follow-up of a count parent offers at least as many options as the parent's largest count.

**Tests, proven non-vacuous by breaking the fix and watching them fail.** New: `checkin-skipped-meals-count-match.test.ts` (22), `checkin-continue-never-silent.test.ts` (18), `checkin-followup-shape-integrity.test.ts` (11, against the real bank). Three existing suites updated for the `required` to `blockedReason` change, strengthened rather than weakened (they now assert a non-empty reason exists, not merely that a flag is true). Deliberate break 1: `requiredSelectionCount` forced to return null — 8 count-match tests failed by name. Deliberate break 2: `continueHelperText` returning null instead of the fallback — the invariant test failed. Deliberate break 3: the local database row reverted to `single_select` with "More than one" — 4 integrity tests failed, including the bug-class assertion. All restored, all green.
